articles.title: Malacañang: Prepare for El Niño, but don't hoard water
articles.summary: Malacañang urged Filipinos to conserve rather than hoard water as the government prepares for an intensified El Niño.

blocks.text: UP Institute of Environmental Science and Meteorology (UPIESM) Assistant Professor Alan Racoma shows the position of the Super El Niño at the Project Noah office, October 1, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang assured the public on Thursday, October 1, that the government has measures in place to prepare for a potentially stronger El Niño, while urging Filipinos not to hoard water.

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the Marcos administration is coordinating with concerned government agencies to prepare for the impacts of the weather phenomenon and has allocated funds for response measures.
"Kumbaga ang El Niño ay hindi na po bago sa Pilipinas. Kung mas matindi lamang po ang magiging epekto ngayon ng El Niño ay dahil dala ng climate change, pero handa po ang gobyerno," Castro said.
("El Niño is not new to the Philippines. If the effects of El Niño are more severe this time because of climate change, the government is prepared.")

PAGASA said a "strong" El Niño is currently affecting the tropical Pacific and is expected to intensify into a "very strong" El Niño between September and December 2026 and persist through the first half of 2027. The weather bureau warned that the phenomenon increases the likelihood of below-normal rainfall, dry spells, drought and water supply stress in parts of the country.

The National Water Resources Board (NWRB) has reduced the allocation for the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System from the usual 50 to 53 cubic meters per second to 44 cubic meters per second starting October as part of measures to conserve water stored in Angat Dam. Irrigation allocation will likewise be cut from 30 to 35 cms to 20 cms.
The Climate Change Commission has also warned that the heat index in cities and towns with limited tree cover could reach 45 to 50 degrees Celsius during the intensified El Niño.
Hoarding 'not advisable'
Castro discouraged the public from hoarding water supplies, particularly bottled drinking water, saying excessive stockpiling could unnecessarily tighten supply and push prices higher.
"Alam niyo naman ang tubig kapag ito ay bottled water, meron din po itong panahon na dapat ito ay i-consume. So hindi po advisable na kayo ay magtago, mag-hoard ng mga tubig ngayon," Castro said.
("As you know, bottled water should also be consumed within a certain period. So it is not advisable to stockpile or hoard water at this time.")
Castro said the government has not received reports of a shortage of bottled drinking water and urged the public to prepare without panic-buying.
She said preparing for possible water shortages is reasonable, but should be done properly, including through water conservation.
"Kaagapay po ninyo ang gobyerno, ang pamahalaan at lahat ng mga concerned agencies. So hindi po kinakailangang mag-panic. Kailangan lang po ng tamang pagprepara," Castro said.
("The government and all concerned agencies are working with you. There is no need to panic. What is needed is proper preparation.")
Task Force El Niño
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. earlier ordered agencies involved in the government's El Niño response to step up preparations, particularly for the agriculture and water sectors.

Marcos reactivated and reconstituted Task Force El Niño through Executive Order 53 in January 2024. The task force was mandated to coordinate government measures on water supply, food security, energy, public health and safety, among other areas.

Castro said Marcos has convened agencies involved in the current preparations, including PAGASA, the Department of Agriculture, National Irrigation Administration, NWRB and Department of Social Welfare and Development.
"Lahat po ito ngayon ay pinapakilos na po," Castro said.
("All these agencies are now being mobilized.")

articles.title: Global bond sell-off intensifies, as UK long-term borrowing costs pass 6%
articles.summary: Fears that US deficit is unsustainable drive Britain’s 30-year bond yield to level not seen since 1998

blocks.text: The turmoil in global bond markets has intensified amid fears the US deficit is reaching unsustainable levels, helping drive UK long-term borrowing costs to a 28-year high.

The threat of a renewed round of inflation from the persistently high cost of oil has spooked investors, who believe central banks will be forced to raise interest rates in the coming months to prevent price increases from becoming embedded.
In a morning of hectic trading on Thursday, the yield, which is a proxy for the interest rate, hit 6% on Britain’s 30-year bonds for the first time since 1998.
The yield on five- and 10-year UK bonds also rose, driving up the government’s borrowing costs and adding to the pressure on the chancellor, John Healey, before the budget later this month.

Stock market investors also sold heavily, knocking 1.7% off the FTSE 100 in London during early trading. Bourses in other parts of Europe were also hit, with Germany’s Dax and France’s CAC 40 falling by 1.1%.

“There is carnage in the bond market which is hitting stocks hard,” said Neil Wilson, the investor strategist at Saxo UK. “It looks like the relentless rout in the bond market is sending investors running for cover.”
The bond sell-off around the world is being driven by fears of high inflation, as the Middle East conflict continues to restrict oil supplies from the region.
On Wednesday, US 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2002, while Japan’s 10-year yield rose towards the 30-year high set last month.

US bonds weakened despite inflation data on Wednesday coming in lower than forecast, which was expected to calm investors’ nerves about the prospect of further increases in the cost of borrowing by the US Federal Reserve.
Traders remain anxious that the Fed will continue to raise interest rates to fight inflation, mainly in response to the strength of the US economy and the prospect of workers bidding up their wages.
after newsletter promotion
Mohit Kumar, an economist at Jefferies, said there was growing concern at the amount of debt being issued to fund government deficits, as well as inflation concerns.
“Inflation, deficit and issuance concerns continue to weigh on the bond market,” he said.

“There is also a buyers’ strike as investors do not want to step in till we get some form of stability. Hedge funds have suffered in the latest round of sell-off and do not have the risk appetite to fade the move. Real money, potentially has the risk appetite, but won’t step in till we get some stability.”

Axel Rudolph, the chief technical analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, said: “While the latest data has reduced expectations of an October Fed rate hike, investors remain wary that persistent inflation and higher oil prices could keep rates elevated for longer.
“The dollar is benefiting from that caution, climbing to a three-month high, while the prospect of a December rate increase keeps pressure on bond markets.”

articles.title: Tennessee governor orders outside review after death row inmate Christa Pike survives execution attempt
articles.summary: Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a classmate three decades ago, survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by means of lethal injection late on Wednesday, prison officials said, foiling the…

image.caption: Witnesses' accounts said Christa Pike was still alive and snoring after executioners injected her with lethal chemicals, according to a federal court motion filed by Pike's lawyers. (J. Miles Cary/ Knoxville News Sentinel/USA Today Network/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a classmate three decades ago, survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by means of lethal injection late on Wednesday, prison officials said, foiling the state's first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries.
It was the 2nd failed execution in Tennessee this year

Pike's condition following the ordeal was not immediately known, and it was not clear what legal avenues her lawyers or the state might pursue next after she was taken for medical treatment from the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.

The Tennessee Department of Correction defended its handling of the high-profile execution, which had been opposed by her lawyers and human rights experts due to Pike's age at the time of the crime, her history as the victim of childhood sexual abuse and untreated mental illness.
"The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the state’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General’s Office," the agency said in a statement.

"The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility," the statement concluded.
Her lawyers said in court filings that officials gave Pike two doses of pentobarbital. Tennessee announced a switch nearly two years ago from a three-drug protocol previously used for executions.

items: After day of delays, witnesses say Tennessee unable to carry out execution of Christa Pike

blocks.text: Governor suspends execution

Pike's lawyers filed a federal court motion during the process seeking to halt her execution, citing witnesses' accounts that "executioners had injected both syringes of lethal injection chemicals and Pike is still alive and snoring," NBC News reported.

Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee, who denied Pike's clemency petition on Monday, said in a statement that he has ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred" and that the remaining scheduled execution will not take place this year.

The failed execution is the second in Tennessee this year, after prison officials in May aborted attempts to execute a man convicted of murders after failing to find a suitable vein for his lethal injection.

The botched attempt on Wednesday came hours after the U.S. Supreme Court lifted an 11th-hour lower-court stay of the execution, clearing the way for Pike, 50, to be put to death for her role in the 1995 torture and beating death of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville.

Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and a third companion lured Slemmer, a classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational centre, into a wooded area where they tortured and killed her.

The grisly nature of the slaying, which involved the perpetrators carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim's chest and taking a chunk of her skull as a souvenir of the carnage, drew intense media coverage at the time.
Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted of first-degree murder.
Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, has spoken out in support of the execution.
Ambulance arrives

Journalists who witnessed the attempted execution described snoring, loud exhales, gasps and complaints from Pike about discomfort in her arm. At times, the curtain was closed and journalists could only hear sounds.
Clergy were called into the chamber twice, they said, before an ambulance was seen arriving at the prison and then leaving.

items: Supreme Court ruling enables midazolam to still be used for executions
Oklahoma releases review after botched injection of death row inmate

blocks.text: Aside from being the first woman the state of Tennessee has tried to execute in more than 200 years, Pike was also poised to become the only person in the modern era of U.S. capital punishment to be executed in Tennessee for a crime committed as a teenager.

In a 226-page petition asking the governor to commute Pike's death penalty to a life sentence without the possibility of parole, her lawyers earlier this week documented her history as the childhood victim of violence, neglect and sexual abuse, including two rapes at ages 11 and 17.
They also cited diagnoses she received in prison for bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder.

Moreover, her lawyers pointed to evidence that Pike's mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for their client to control her impulses as a young person.
Pike was also convicted in August 2001 of attempted first-degree murder in an assault on another inmate, according to the Correction Department.

Executions of female prison inmates are exceedingly rare in the U.S., with women accounting for just 18 of the 1,683 people put to death since the Supreme Court allowed capital punishment to resume in 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.
Before Wednesday, Tennessee had executed 17 people.
With files from The Associated Press and CBC News

articles.title: Tennessee governor halts executions after second botched lethal injection attempt this year – US politics live
articles.summary: Bill Lee pauses state’s remaining executions for the rest of the year after inmate Christa Pike survives two lethal injections

blocks.text: Tennessee governor halts executions after second botched lethal injection attempt this year
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Tennessee governor Bill Lee has halted the state’s remaining executions for the rest of the year after officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death yesterday.

Pike, 50, was alive and loudly snoring after the attempted lethal injection and taken by ambulance from the prison, her attorneys said. She was being treated at a hospital, but they said they hadn’t been told about her condition.
She had been scheduled for execution at 10am on Wednesday for the killing she committed at age 18 and would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.
Governor Lee said that he was halting the one remaining execution for the rest of 2026 and ordered a “comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred.”

“Carrying out a lawfully imposed sentence is among the State’s most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective,” Lee said in a statement.
The Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement that they “followed every step of the State’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General’s Office.”

Officials gave Pike two doses of pentobarbital, her attorneys said in court filings late Wednesday. The state’s execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes to be administered “if the inmate is not deceased” after the first set. It does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set.

It was the second time this year that Tennessee has been unable to carry out an execution. In May, state officials called off the lethal injection of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and killing three people in 1994, after executioners tried and failed for over an hour to place an IV to administer pentobarbital.

blocks.text: Trump officials abandon effort to investigate election threats, experts warn

blocks.caption: George Chidi

blocks.text: George Chidi

The Trump administration has abandoned key security bodies meant to investigate direct threats to US elections by foreign actors and domestic terrorists, according to former officials and a recent report.

While administration officials have been actively focused on unsubstantiated claims of widespread voter fraud by noncitizens, other credible election threats appear to have been overlooked, the officials say.

Between 2021 and 2024, the justice department’s election threats taskforce prosecuted 21 cases, like that of Solomon Peña, a failed candidate for the New Mexico house of representatives who organized shootings at the houses of election officials, or Quintez Brown, who shot up a campaign meeting of Louisville’s mayor.

Democrats and Republicans faced prosecution for harassing, intimidating and threatening elections workers, noted Nikki Fisher, former chief election security officer for the Oregon secretary of state, now the executive director of the Oregon District Attorneys Association.
Since then, the taskforce seems to have gone quiet.

“While officials are being trained to handle threats, the federal deterrent meant to punish the people making them appears to have gone quiet,” Fisher said. “To date, no new cases have been prosecuted, and the DoJ’s election threats taskforce appears to be defunct in practice.”

articles.title: Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims his Germany team are ‘not white enough’
articles.summary:
• He says social media claims are ‘nonsense’ and ‘idiocy’

  • Manager sees ‘no reason to pay attention to these people’

Jürgen Klopp has reacted with disgust to a…

blocks.text: Jürgen Klopp has reacted with disgust to a social media debate questioning whether the Germany team he is in the process of forming are “white enough”.
Klopp said he believed there was no point in giving room to “such people and their utterances”, dismissing them as “complete nonsense”.

Asked in a press conference to respond to the debate as to whether the national team were “not German enough” or “not white enough”, he said: “There is absolutely no reason to pay attention to these people. You won’t get my thoughts on this. I have little time in everyday life for idiocy – and even less on social media.
“The great crux of our lives is that everyone is allowed to express their opinion … it’s insane when something like that exists.”

Klopp said that watching sportspeople interact with each other was proof to him that mutual respect was still possible. “The world could learn a thing or two from a sports changing room … There, everyone is respected based on the facts and not discredited based on false opinions. Full stop.”

Klopp, whose plans for the Germany team since he took over as the manager in the summer have attracted huge attention, said the players he had gathered at the national team camp, including several players with a migrant background, “could not be better united than they are”.

The barrage of racist and generally offensive commentaries on social media followed Germany’s 1-0 defeat by Greece last Sunday, in the Nations League, marking the first time Greece had defeated Germany.

It is also reflective of plenty of utterances from MPs of the far-right populist Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), the largest opposition party in the Bundestag, who have repeatedly and consistently criticised the diversity and ethnic makeup of the national team, often referring to the squad in derogatory terms such as a “politically correct mercenary force”.
after newsletter promotion
Klopp, who has a four-year contract running until the end of the 2030 World Cup, was speaking before Germany’s Nations League match on Thursday evening against Serbia.

articles.title: UAE launches flydubai hijacking and terrorism investigation
articles.summary: The UAE's chief prosecutor said it's looking at the possibility of "terrorist activity or intent" in the alleged attempted hijacking of a flydubai commercial flight to Tel Aviv. It says it has…

image.caption: A replacement plane brought the passengers safely to Ben Gurion airport late on Wednesday Image: Gil Cohen-Magen/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The United Arab Emirates' chief prosecutor's office said on Thursday that it had ordered an investigation into the apparent attempt to hijack and possibly crash a flydubai flight to Israel a day earlier.

The state news agency WAM said that "the investigation team has launched its work into the incident already" and that the probe would seek to determine "the degree to which [the incident] was linked to any terrorist activity or intent."
The case will also seek to establish whether it was a pre-meditated and planned incident involving other actors or the work of a lone perpetrator.
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz had called the emergency on the flight to Tel Aviv "an attempted jihadist terror attack" that was thwarted.
Passengers described rushing the cockpit to assist the pilot after he was stabbed by his copilot, who then put the plane into a steep dive in an apparent attempt to crash the airliner.
Aside from minor curts and bruises among those who intervened in the cockpit, the passengers — the vast majority of whom were Israeli — were all unhurt.

blocks.caption: Israeli passengers returned home late on Wednesday after the near-missImage: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Why does the UAE have jurisdiction in the case?
Judicial authorities in the UAE have jurisdiction over the incident.

This is because the aircraft is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag, the statement said, adding that UAE law applied to crimes committed on board "even if they occur outside the country's territory."

The plane was over northern Saudi Arabia for the majority of the early-morning security incident, with tracking data suggesting it briefly crossed into Jordan before turning around to make an emergency landing at the nearby Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia.
FlyDubai passengers recount terror after hijacking attempt
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had also indicated the likelihood of the UAE leading any investigation in a TV interview with Fox News.

"The attacking pilot is ... now being investigated in Saudi Arabia. I think he'll be taken to the Emirates, where he comes from, or at least where he left, where he flew off from, and we'll be following and possibly also participating in this investigation," Netanyahu said.

The Omani copilot's identity has not been made public as yet and his motive is not clear. US President Donald Trump said that based on a discussion with Netanyahu, he understood that the suspect was "perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack-job."
Asked about the possibility of Iranian involvement amid the conflict in the Gulf, Netanyahu said "it's too early to say."

blocks.caption: Israeli leaders spoke to the passengers who intervened in the cockpit, like Yaniv Hayoun speaking here to Prime Minister Benjamin NetanyahuImage: GPO/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Israel's Herzog nominates 4 passengers for presidential medal
Israeli President Isaac Herzog plans to nominate four passengers who helped overpower the attacker for the Presidential Medal for Civil Courage.
Herzog and Netanyahu spoke with the passengers when they arrived at Ben Gurion Airport on a replacement flight late on Wednesday.
Herzog named the passengers as Yaniv Hayoun, Shota Musayev, Zvika Manes and Asaf Rajuan.
"You put yourselves at risk to save others and prevented a terrible disater," Herzog said. "Today, the whole world saw the beautiful and courageous face of Israeli society."
The medal is Israel's highest civilian award for heroism. Herzog confers the medal but typically nominees are formally chosen by a committee.
Musayev, a dentist who administered first aid to the severely wounded Indian pilot, told Herzog everyone on board had acted courageously.
"We supported one another on the plane and also when we arrived in Saudi Arabia, and we took care of each other as we should," he said.

blocks.caption: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu hailed Captain Smit Machchhar's 'extraordinary bravery'Image: Israel's Foreign Ministry/AFP

blocks.text: The Indian captain, Smit Machchhar, has also received staunch praise from Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and from India's Narendra Modi. Passengers described how the pilot fought off his attacker despite his wounds and was able to open the cockpit door to let them in to aid him. He was in a stable condition in a Saudi hospital, India's Embassy in Riyadh said on Wednesday.

"In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others," Modi said online. "His valor helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy."

articles.title: Why is Rosary Month celebrated in October?
articles.summary: As the Catholic Church dedicates the entire month of October to praying the Rosary, the faithful are urged to seek the intercession of the Our Lady of the Rosary and contemplate the life of Jesus…

blocks.text: As the Catholic Church dedicates the entire month of October to praying the Rosary, the faithful are urged to seek the intercession of the Our Lady of the Rosary and contemplate the life of Jesus Christ through the mysteries.
During his Apostolic Journey to France, Pope Leo XIV urged the faithful to pray the Rosary for peace, particularly in the world’s conflict areas.
“Let us accompany this prayer with concrete acts of penance and mercy, committing ourselves always to fostering dialogue and reconciliation,” the Pontiff said.
But why is the Rosary Month celebrated in October, and how did the veneration of the Marian image begin in the Philippines?
An October victory

Pope Pius V established the feast of the Our Lady of Victory, the name of the Our Lady of the Rosary then, on October 7, 1571, after Christian forces won a battle against the Ottoman Empire in the Gulf of Patras in western Greece.
The victory weakened the Ottoman Empire’s westward expansion and helped prevent its potential conquest of Christian Europe.

In an interview, historian Br. Dennis Amarante, O.P., of the Order of Preachers, said Pope Pius V asked the faithful to seek the Blessed Virgin Mary’s intercession for the victory of Christian forces by praying the Rosary.

“Pope Pius V, who was a Dominican, asked the people, and he himself, prayed the Rosary to ask the intercession of the Blessed Mother in order for the Christian forces to prevail,” Amarante told GMA News Online.
“And they did prevail. So they won the naval battle. And as a result, in thanksgiving, Pope Pius V instituted October 7 to be the feast of Our Lady of the Rosary,” he added.
In 1573, Pope Gregory XIII changed the name of the feast from Our Lady of Victory to the Feast of the Holy Rosary to honor the power of the Rosary used during that battle.
Since the Feast of Our Lady of the Rosary falls in October, the entire month eventually became known as the Rosary Month.
Filipinos’ faith in the Rosary
After the victory in the Battle of Lepanto, the praying of the Rosary was soon introduced in the Philippines after the Order of the Preachers (Dominicans) arrived in the country in 1587.

"One of those missionaries who came to the Philippines was the Dominicans, and being the primary propagators of the Holy Rosary, they brought the veneration to the Marian image in the country,” Amarante said.
He shared that when the Dominicans arrived in the Philippines, they brought a statue of Our Lady of the Rosary and housed it in the Sto. Domingo Church in Intramuros, Manila.

“When Santo Domingo Church was still standing in Intramuros, it was there in the façade. Unfortunately, one of the casualties of the Second World War,” said Amarante, who published articles and conference papers on Philippine Church history, Philippine Dominican history, and historical methodology.

An image of Sto. Domingo Church in Intramuros, Manila, before it was destroyed during the bombing in World War II. The image is displayed at the Museo de Santo Domingo in Quezon City. Mariel Celine Serquiña/GMA News
For Catholics, praying the Rosary is a way to seek healing, solace, and comfort while reflecting on the life of Jesus Christ.
The Rosary is divided into four sets of mysteries: the Joyful, Sorrowful, Luminous, and Glorious Mysteries. Each set consists of five events from the life of Jesus Christ.
As they meditate on each mystery, Catholics pray the Hail Mary 10 times, followed by one Glory Be.

For Amarante, despite the Marian image’s Western iconography, it eventually took on a local context in the Philippines, with devotions to Our Lady of La Naval de Manila in Quezon City, Our Lady of Manaoag in Pangasinan, and Our Lady of the Rosary of Orani in Bataan, among others.
"Eventually, over time, it would have a significant effect on the lives of Filipinos. Filipinos would eventually call her their own,” Amarante explained.
One reason, the Dominican brother said, is that the Marian image “transcended the bounds of the context” to which Filipinos can relate.

“They see not just a Western icon or statue, but they see it as a representation of the Blessed Mother who is there with them despite challenges and tribulations, guiding them towards her Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. Each of them would carry their own prayers of supplication,” Amarante said.
Lessons from Our Lady of the Rosary
Like the Blessed Virgin Mary, Amarante challenged the faithful to be courageous in doing good and be devoted to God and his teachings.
"Pinakita ng Mahal na Ina na kahit na maraming pagsubok, kahit na ang daming pagihirap, dumipende siya sa kanyang pananampalatay sa Diyos," Amarante said.
(The Blessed Mother showed that despite the many trials and hardships, she relied on her faith in God.)
"Ginawa niya ang tama, sumunod siya, at namuhay siya bilang isang mabuting hapo, isang mabuting ina, isang mabuting pananampalatay," he added.
(She did what was right, obeyed, and lived as a good person, a good mother, and a woman of faith.)
In a time where there is violence, division, dishonesty, and disregard for what is right, Amarante said it's easy to show "religious fervor."
"Sa panahon ngayon, ang dali-daling mag debosyon, ang dali-daling magpakita ng religious fervor, we always depend on the externalities of things," the Dominican brother said.
(In these times, it is easy to practice devotion and show religious fervor, but we often rely too much on the external aspects of our faith.)

"So sana, sa patuloy nating pamumuhay bilang mga Kristiyano na may debosyon sa Mahal na Birheng Maria, sana yung mga lessons na yun maglulot sa atin ang internal transformation, conversion," he added.
(So, as we continue to live as Christians devoted to the Blessed Virgin Mary, may the lessons we learn from these devotions lead to an internal transformation and conversion.)
Follow facebook.com/gmanewsonline for real-time news and developments in the Philippines and around the world.—RF, GMA News

items: Filipina tennis player Alex Eala won a bronze medal at the 2026 Asian Games after losing in the semifinals to China's Wang Xiyu.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Another one of the Philippines’ top gold-medal bets in the 2026 Asian Games fell as tennis star Alex Eala settled for a bronze on Thursday, October 1.

For the second straight edition, the Filipina ran into a Chinese wall, suffering a 3-6, 6-3, 6-2 loss to Wang Xiyu in the semifinals of the women’s singles at the Higashiyama Park Tennis Center in Nagoya, Japan.
“A lot of good points, a lot of tough moments for me. I think in the end, she played better. Have to sit and think about it,” Eala told Filipino reporters.
Eala replicated her bronze finish in 2023 in Hangzhou, China, where she also lost in the semifinals to Chinese star and eventual champion Zheng Qinwen.
This time, though, expectations and scenarios were different as Eala came in as the highest-ranked player in the field at world No. 18, even earning a first-round bye as the top seed.
And Eala lived up to her billing at the start, racing to a 5-0 lead before holding off a Wang comeback to clinch the opening set.
But Wang, ranked 85th in the world, proved to be no pushover as she won the second set to force a decider and went on to complete the upset victory in 2 hours and 34 minutes.
Down 1-4 in the third set, Eala showed signs of life by breaking Wang in the sixth game, but that only delayed her exit as the Chinese won the next two games to seal the win.
A forehand error by Eala marked the end of her gold bid.

It was a disappointing result for Eala, considering she entered the tournament as the title favorite, with the likes of Zheng, world No. 1 Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan, and world No. 17 Naomi Osaka of Japan skipping the Asian Games to compete in the China Open.

The loss denied Eala a shot at becoming the first Filipino tennis champion in the Asian Games since Johnny Jose ruled the men’s singles in 1962. It also denied Eala a direct entry in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
But as dismayed as she is, Eala relished the opportunity of representing the country again in a multi-sport showdown.

“It meant a lot to me to be here and to compete. At the end of the day, I gave my all. I prepped the best I could prep. I fought the best I could fight. Happy that I was able to have this experience,” she said.
Up next for Eala is the Wuhan Open that kicks off in China on October 12. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Trump officials abandon effort to investigate election threats, experts warn
articles.summary:
Credible threats appear to have been overlooked as administration focuses on unverified claims of voter fraud

The Trump administration has abandoned key security bodies meant to investigate…

blocks.text: The Trump administration has abandoned key security bodies meant to investigate direct threats to US elections by foreign actors and domestic terrorists, according to former officials and a recent report.

While administration officials have been actively focused on unsubstantiated claims of widespread voter fraud by noncitizens, other credible election threats appear to have been overlooked, the officials say.

Between 2021 and 2024, the justice department’s election threats taskforce prosecuted 21 cases, like that of Solomon Peña, a failed candidate for the New Mexico house of representatives who organized shootings at the houses of election officials, or Quintez Brown, who shot up a campaign meeting of Louisville’s mayor.

Democrats and Republicans faced prosecution for harassing, intimidating and threatening elections workers, noted Nikki Fisher, former chief election security officer for the Oregon secretary of state, now the executive director of the Oregon District Attorneys Association.
Since then, the taskforce seems to have gone quiet.

“While officials are being trained to handle threats, the federal deterrent meant to punish the people making them appears to have gone quiet,” Fisher said. “To date, no new cases have been prosecuted, and the DoJ’s election threats taskforce appears to be defunct in practice.”

Contacted for comment on the status of the election threats taskforce, the justice department referred to a series of nine DoJ media releases over the past five weeks describing indictments of foreign nationals on charges of election fraud and stolen identities.

In an academic paper published in June, while she was studying at the Naval Postgraduate School, Fisher noted that the taskforce received more than 2,000 reports of election threats between 2021 and 2024. It opened more than 100 investigations into those threats.

Trump administration officials began disbanding election investigative groups within the justice department, the office of the director of national intelligence, and other agencies almost immediately after the president started his second term.

The first day after Pam Bondi won Senate confirmation as attorney general, she eliminated the FBI’s foreign influence taskforce, which had been investigating influence campaigns waged by China, Russia and other adversaries.

Administration leaders fired or reassigned personnel working on foreign election interference at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (Cisa). They also defunded Cisa’s training program for local officials to monitor and coordinate threats through the Elections Infrastructure Information Sharing and Analysis Center.
Pleas from Democratic lawmakers during budget negotiations in 2025 to retain the task force and other election integrity assets went unheeded.

“I’m less worried about jurisdictions’ ability to defend themselves in particular,” said Geoff Hale, a visiting fellow for election security at the Center for Democracy & Technology and former director at Cisa. “I’m more worried about the lack of an information-sharing environment across the community.”

Federal cuts to these agencies’ monitoring and investigative apparatus leaves local agencies blind to broader patterns, he said. “The relationships and trust that Cisa had built up over 10 years, that was how the tapestry of security professionals that support elections across the country stayed in close contact and were able to close vulnerabilities to keep events and incidents from occurring in multiple locations.”

Agencies working together with state and local election leaders offered regular warnings about suspicious activity, said Caitlin Durkovich, a former deputy homeland security adviser for resilience and response on the national security council, said at a briefing staged by the Brennan Center for Justice last week.

“This administration … has dismantled the entire apparatus that is responsible for detecting and holding these bad actors accountable,” she said. “That has all gone away at a moment when this administration is again claiming that the spectre of foreign operations is … in play.”
Meanwhile, Trump officials have been focused on some of the president’s longstanding personal grievances when it comes to election integrity.

FBI agents swooped into Fulton county in January to seize ballots from the 2020 election, ostensibly as part of a continuing investigation into foreign election interference. Tulsi Gabbard, then the director of national intelligence, was present at the FBI raid. Similarly, the ODNI and the FBI seized elections apparatus in Puerto Rico, again while investigating foreign interference.
Nothing has yet come of either event.

But both cases led up to a primetime address by Trump on 16 July, where he claimed China had acquired extensive voter information during the 2020 election cycle, characterizing it as an effort to influence and undermine legitimacy in the 2018 midterm and 2020 presidential elections.

Trump argued that US election databases and hardware had vulnerabilities to foreign adversaries, and that Venezuela had digitally manipulated its election results in ways that might be replicated in an American election.
Trump’s claims could not be substantiated from the evidence presented.
Since that address – and the public’s tepid response to the claims – the administration has pivoted to a dogged pursuit of noncitizen voters in American elections.

The DoJ has charged more than 90 people with voter-related fraud offenses, 50 noncitizens in the last five weeks, attorney general Todd Blanche said on Wednesday, contrasting it with 13 cases brought under the Biden administration.

“What we do at Department of Homeland Security is not controversial; we’re enforcing our nation’s laws,” said homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin, who was also at the event. “Underneath the Trump administration, we will always protect the integrity of our election system and enforce our nation’s laws.”

articles.title: [READOUT] What Philippine borrowing tells businesses ahead of 2027
articles.summary: Here are three credit insights to keep in mind, covering consumer borrowing trends, business lending, and the national debt

blocks.text: It turns out whether you’re running a household or the country, debt is becoming a bigger part of the picture. For businesses though, what matters more than the mere fact that borrowing is rising is what that debt is being used for and whether enough value is generated in return.
Here are three points worth watching as you plan for 2027.

First, credit is becoming an important cash flow tool for Filipino consumers amid a challenging economic environment, and this could have implications for what payment options retailers should prioritize offering.

Rappler sat down one-on-one with Peter Faulhaber, president and CEO of TransUnion Philippines, whose latest Credit Perception Index reached a record 75 as Filipinos became more knowledgeable, trusting, and favorable toward credit overall.

But this growing comfort with borrowing is happening with a still-cautious consumer. TransUnion’s report found respondents less confident about their own finances over the next three months and one year. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) Q3 survey also showed consumers had weaker plans for day-to-day household spending even as their expectations for future income and employment improved.

A deeper look into the lending data helps explain how those two things can coexist. The BSP found that credit card receivables jumped 24.9% year on year to P1.3 trillion in July and salary-based general purpose loans rose 15.7%, while motor-vehicle loans grew just 4.5%. TransUnion, meanwhile, reported that buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) products had the strongest growth in adoption, with what Faulhaber called a “large take-up rate” and “strong favorability.”

The emerging picture: cash-strapped consumers may be using shorter-term loans to manage when expenses are paid, rather than simply to fund large purchases. Around 59% of credit users told TransUnion they borrow for emergency expenses, ahead of personal expenses and utility bills, a pattern Faulhaber described as a sign of greater maturity.

For retailers, that may mean rethinking which payment options get the most emphasis. BNPL, installments, and cards can help customers manage tight cash flow and avoid delaying a purchase. Some 43% of Filipinos surveyed said they plan to borrow or use credit to make purchases, up 5 percentage points from last year. BNPL was the credit product most commonly viewed as “helpful” at 54%, ahead of credit cards at 49%. Cost could limit uptake, however, with 54% citing high interest rates as a reason to avoid credit.
Second, in today’s difficult macroeconomic environment, business credit has become selective, but not weak.

Production loans remain almost five times larger than consumer credit at P13.2 trillion and account for roughly three-fourths of local bank lending, according to BSP data. But the fastest growth is concentrated only in particular parts of the economy:

items: Fastest growth came from infrastructure-linked industries. Water and waste loans rose 26.2%, transport and storage 25.1%, electricity and gas 24.4%, and accommodation and food services 16.3%.
The biggest loan books grew more slowly. Real estate rose 5.5% to P2.89 trillion, wholesale and retail 8.8% to P1.64 trillion, and manufacturing 7.2% to P1.28 trillion.
Construction was the clear weak spot. Loans fell 13.3% year on year to P447.5 billion.

blocks.text: Third, keep an eye on the national debt and how it could tighten fiscal space for everyone.

National government debt stood at P19.39 trillion in July, while financial expenses in the proposed 2027 budget reached P1.114 trillion. Neither the World Bank nor the economists Rappler spoke with sees an immediate debt crisis, given that much of Philippine debt is long-term, domestic, and peso-denominated.

The concern for business is the squeeze on fiscal space. Interest costs have risen from around 10% of government spending before the pandemic to about 16.7% today, leaving the Marcos administration less room to fund infrastructure and other projects that might have otherwise improved private sector productivity.

Rappler resident economist JC Punongbayan puts it neatly. “Borrowing for productive investments is defensible, but borrowing for overpriced, substandard, or ghost projects only worsens the debt problem.”
We hope this readout helps inform your next strategy or boardroom decision. And as always, feel free to tell us what to tackle next, dear business leader. – Rappler.com

Readout is a new content series from data consultancy The Nerve, bringing you insights that bridge the gap between quick news headlines and dense technical reports. Readout tracks and explains business shifts in different Philippine industries. Crafted from on-the-ground reporting and data-driven analyses, Readout provides a clear read on where market and consumption are headed, what’s shaping demand across different sectors, who the key players are, and why it all matters.

articles.title: Were prosecutors even on the same page when Trillanes was dropped as witness?
articles.summary: From our candid conversations with some prosecution panel members, it appears that Luistro's manifestation to drop Trillanes caught them off-guard

blocks.text: Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV was expected to be a crucial figure in the prosecution’s unexplained wealth case against Vice President Sara Duterte, until he was unceremoniously dropped from the witness list on Thursday, October 1.

Trillanes later said the withdrawal of his name from the prosecution’s witness lineup was his own decision, but it doesn’t take a genius reporter to notice the disarray surrounding the surprise disclosure of lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro in open court.

After the announcement, no lawmaker or private lawyer sat in the scheduled daily press conference of the prosecution panel — the first time its lunch-time media briefing was canceled for undisclosed reasons since the trial commenced in July.
Most of the prosecution panel members declined media interviews during the break, and when one — prosecutor Keith Flores — heeded journalists’ request, he couldn’t double down on Luistro’s statement.
“I really could not say,” Flores said when asked if the decision to let go of Trillanes as a witness was final.
At 2:43 pm, Trillanes posted a statement on Facebook in an apparent bid to reclaim the narrative.

“Earlier in the day, I requested the House prosecution under Chair Jinky Luistro to formally withdraw my name as a witness for the prosecution. This way, the prosecution panel would be relieved from the pressure it is going through,” he said.
So, what gives?
From our candid conversations with some prosecution panel members, it appears that Luistro’s manifestation to drop Trillanes caught them off-guard.

“I was also just informed about the decision earlier today. In fact, in the interviews we were giving prior to that, our assumption was that he will still be presented as a witness,” private prosecutor Jay Tolosa said in a Rappler interview.

Luistro herself said that she was informed by Trillanes about his decision to withdraw, but she couldn’t say who else in the team were informed before she made the disclosure at the impeachment court.
Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan alluded to the reluctance of senator-judges, which supposedly informed Trillanes’ decision to back out.
“We were surprised, and I guess because that was his personal decision in consideration of the hesitancy of the senators,” Kapunan said.

Trillanes has a complicated if not rocky history with some of his former colleagues in the upper chamber. Online, Trillanes’ past comments about presiding officer Chiz Escudero’s supposed questionable wealth resurfaced in the run-up to his supposed court appearance.

blocks.caption: Were prosecutors even on the same page when Trillanes was dropped as witness?

blocks.text: At the post-trial conference on Thursday, the prosecutors stuck to a line of messaging: Trillanes’ decision to withdraw was his, and there’s nothing they can do.

It’s a bizarre explanation, given that the prosecution had hyped up his testimony for months. If Trillanes really requested to have his name withdrawn, the prosecution could have convinced him that such a concern was unwarranted.
“Our parting statement is let us watch (former) senator Trillanes’ press conference tomorrow,” Luistro said.

blocks.caption: Were prosecutors even on the same page when Trillanes was dropped as witness?

articles.title: Germans' biggest fear is the high cost of living, an annual study finds
articles.summary: What do Germans fear most in 2026? Wars? Global crises? Wrong. Their biggest concern is the cost of living, which keeps rising.

image.caption: Germans see the price of groceries, energy risingImage: Frank Hoermann/SvenSimon/picture alliance

blocks.text: People in Germany are more politically engaged than they have been in a long time. This was also evident in the high voter turnout in the September state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
Germans are passionately debating immigration, the upcoming reforms to pensions, healthcare and long-term care, as well as democracy and the rule of law.

But by far their greatest fear is the cost of living in Germany, which is becoming increasingly expensive. At least, that is the finding of the 2026 study on "Germans' Fears," which the insurer R+V presented in Berlin.
From early May through late July of this year, researchers surveyed some 2,400 German-speaking citizens aged 14 and older.
The cost of living is again their top concern, as it has been in the survey for many years in a row. This study has been conducted annually since the early 1990s.
Last year, 52% of those polled cited the rising cost of daily life as their greatest concern; in 2026, that figure has risen to 59%.
At a press conference in Berlin, Isabelle Borucki, a political scientist from Marburg who served as a consultant on the study, explained why.
"The price of key items — energy, housing and food — has risen noticeably. This reduces the financial leeway for leisure, vacations and purchases. People can afford less and less."
Germans worry about higher taxes and contributions
The study also shows that people are well aware that Germany's social security systems are in a serious crisis. Both the state pension fund and long-term care insurance are chronically in the red.
Most people also seem to realize that taxes and contributions will rise. That is why the fear of higher taxes is stronger than in previous years.

"Behind the fear of higher taxes and benefit cuts lies the question of fairness, with people wondering who will bear the costs of modernization," Borucki said. "And they worry, 'Can I still rely on getting benefits I am entitled to?'"
Less fear of war, immigration and Donald Trump
But what about the issues that are also dominating the headlines in Germany? What about immigration and the increasing polarization of society? Or global upheavals?
A narrow majority of 52% of those surveyed fear that the number of refugees is overwhelming the German state. This fear ranks third among all concerns.
But when it comes to global upheavals, Germans are not so concerned.
Only 45% of respondents fear that US President Donald Trump's policies are making the world a more dangerous place, researcher Grischa Brower-Rabinowitsch said.
"That's significantly fewer than during his first term."

In 2018, during Trump's first term, 69% responded to the same question by saying that this made them very afraid. "After years of constant geopolitical alarm bells, people are starting to get used to it," Brower-Rabinowitsch said.
Berlin has space, so why is housing so expensive?
German politicians got poor grades

This trend also seems to hold true for other areas of concern: Germans are looking to the future with considerably less anxiety than expected. Only 34% now fear a war involving Germany, down from 41% last year.

Since 1992, the study has asked people if they are afraid of losing their job? Currently, only 20% of the surveyed members of the working population answered "yes." That is the lowest figure ever recorded.

However, the assessment of politicians — both those in the government and those in the opposition — is sobering: Respondents were asked to grade politicians with one being the best and six the worst (the grading system used at German schools). The result was an average score of 4.1, which is barely a passing mark.

Political scientist Borucki places the primary responsibility on the current government of conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) under Chancellor Friedrich Merz which came to power in May 2025.
After the end of the previous coalition government, many associated the new coalition with hopes for more leadership, less conflict and a rapid economic turnaround.
"That has not come to pass," says Borucki. "There is now a gap between the grand announcements and tangible results. People are disappointed and losing confidence."
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Quote card of Mark Zuckerberg threatening DICT, House with lawsuit is fake
articles.summary: Neither Zuckerberg nor Meta issued such a statement; the fake quote card circulated amid child safety concerns on Meta's platforms

blocks.text: Claim: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said he would slap the Philippines’ Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and the House of Representatives with a lawsuit.

Why we fact-checked this: A quote card attributed to Zuckerberg, dated September 17, reads: “U.S. government nga nahihirapan sakin e tapos kayo pa kaya dyan sa DICT at House na akala mo naman may tira? Pag sasampalin ko kayo ng mga abogado ko e.”
(Even the US government is having a hard time with me; you people at the DICT and the House think you have a shot at me? I’ll slap you with my lawyers.)
The card adds: “Bilhin ko pa yang House at DICT na yan e (I could just buy the House and DICT).”
The quote card has gone viral on Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram. The most popular Facebook reel drew 2,000 reactions, 120 comments, 310 shares, and 154,000 views as of writing.
Many commenters appeared to take the card as real, praising Zuckerberg for his remarks.
The quote card appears to stem from earlier reports that the House summoned Zuckerberg to address concerns regarding child safety on Meta’s platforms, which the DICT later retracted.
The facts: There is no record of Zuckerberg or Meta issuing this statement on their official channels, including on Meta’s Newsroom.
The quote card also bears the watermark @BalitaNikumparengJeff. Searching for this account leads to the original post, which carries a #satire hashtag in its caption.
Other versions of the viral graphic have no such label.

The card’s premise of a supposed lawsuit threat from the Meta CEO is also unsupported, as the DICT walked back its earlier claim that the House had called on Zuckerberg to appear before lawmakers. On September 21, the DICT clarified that no House resolution was issued directing or inviting Meta or Zuckerberg to appear before the House.

Meta under scrutiny: Meta has faced criticism in the Philippines over incidents of school violence this year. It drew flak for failing to promptly remove the livestream of the August 18 Zamboanga school shooting, which stayed up for about 14 minutes.
On September 16, House lawmakers flagged concerns about harmful online content following the school shootings in Tacloban City and Zamboanga City, and deferred action on the DICT’s 2027 budget.

According to the DICT, the unresolved issues involving the Meta platform include online sexual abuse and exploitation of children and child sexual abuse and exploitation materials. Further harms were also being facilitated or amplified on major platforms, including online illegal gambling, cyberbullying, social media addiction, depression, and related mental health risks, according to the department.

Debunked: This is not the first fabricated Zuckerberg statement to circulate online. A fake letter he supposedly wrote for House lawmakers was first published by the satire site The Adobo Chronicles on September 18. VERA Files rated it as satire, and Rappler debunked the fake letter after several users reposted it without a satire label.
Rappler has previously debunked related false claims about Zuckerberg, Facebook restrictions, and fabricated quote cards:

items: FACT CHECK: No letter from Meta’s Zuckerberg to House lawmakers on social media safety
FACT CHECK: No nationwide Facebook ban set to take effect on September 10
FACT CHECK: No order from Cagayan de Oro mayor Uy banning Muslims from schools
FALSE: Grace Poe to file bill blocking Facebook in light of ABS-CBN shutdown
FACT CHECK: Is Grace Poe pushing for a Facebook ban in PH?

blocks.text: – James Bones/Rappler.com
James Bones is a Research and Data volunteer at Rappler. He is a fourth-year Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering student at the Polytechnic University of the Philippines – Manila.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: DOJ 'almost ready' to file Quiboloy extradition
articles.summary: DOJ enters stage of final review before seeking Quiboloy extradition.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice is nearly ready to file the petition seeking the extradition of doomsday preacher Apollo Quiboloy to the United States.
Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida said Thursday, October 1, that the department is in the final stages of vetting the petition and is conducting a final legal review.
"We're in the final stages already of the vetting. Nagli-legal scrubbing na lang kami. We're almost ready to file that petition," Vida said.
("We're already in the final stages of the vetting process. We're just conducting a legal review now. We're almost ready to file that petition.")
Vida said the Philippines would strictly comply with its obligations under its extradition treaty with the United States.
Asked when the petition would be filed before the extradition court, Vida declined to give a specific date.
Charges in the U.S.
The U.S. government has requested Quiboloy's extradition to face charges in the United States.
Quiboloy, who is also facing qualified human trafficking, child abuse and sexual abuse charges in the Philippines, was indicted by a U.S. federal grand jury in 2021.
The U.S. charges include conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, and sex trafficking of children.
He also faces substantive sex trafficking, conspiracy and bulk cash smuggling charges, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
U.S. prosecutors have accused Quiboloy and other Kingdom of Jesus Christ officials of recruiting women and girls to serve as his personal assistants and coercing them into sex.
Quiboloy has denied the allegations.

articles.title: 19 ride-hailing firms summoned over alleged failure to implement fare hike
articles.summary: Nineteen transport network companies have been summoned after allegedly refusing to comply with the mandated fare increase for transport network vehicle service (TNVS).

blocks.text: Gas station attendants refuel vehicles in Quezon City on March 2, 2026, a day ahead of the expected oil price hike.
The STAR / Michael Varcas
MANILA, Philippines — Nineteen transport network companies (TNCs) have been summoned after allegedly refusing to comply with the mandated fare increase for transport network vehicle service (TNVS).
In a press release on Thursday, October 1, the Land Transportation and Franchising Regulatory Board (LTFRB) said show-cause orders were issued after the agency received complaints from drivers.

The agency ordered the platform providers to submit a written explanation within three working days after receiving the orders as to why their accreditation and authority to operate should not be suspended or canceled.
The hearing is scheduled for Wednesday next week, October 7.
While the LTFRB did not identify the TNCs involved, the agency said ride-hailing drivers are complaining that the platform providers are not fully implementing the government-approved fare increase.
Based on the latest fare hike, the base fare for TNVS went up by P20, raising the new fare for sedans to P65, AUVs/SUVs to P75, hatchbacks to P55, and premium vehicles to P165.
It also set the pickup fare at P15 per kilometer.
The agency said the TNCs reportedly continue to use the old fare system instead of implementing the new one.
According to LTFRB Chairman Greg G. Pua Jr., the TNCs' alleged refusal to implement the fare hike has defeated the agency’s intention in approving the increase.

“Para sa kaalaman ng lahat, ang TNVS partner po ang gumagastos sa gasolina at diesel, at hindi ang mga TNCs. Kaya kapag hindi na-implement ang fare increase para sa kanila, sila po ang maaapektuhan at hindi ang mga TNCs,” Pua said in the statement.
(For everyone’s information, the TNVS partner pays for gasoline and diesel, not the TNCs. So if the fare hike is not implemented for them, they will suffer, not the TNCs.)

articles.title: Pakistan launches deadly airstrikes on Afghanistan
articles.summary: The Taliban government in Afghanistan said at least nine civilians were killed in Pakistani airstrikes on two provinces overnight. Pakistan said it had struck militant hideouts, killing 22 fighters.

image.caption: The Taliban said civilian homes were struckImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: Pakistan launched airstrikes overnight on two provinces in neighboring Afghanistan, the two countries said Thursday.
The Taliban government in Kabul said at least nine civilians, all women and children, were killed, while 11 others were wounded.
Pakistani authorities, on the other hand, said the strikes had killed 22 militants. Neither casualty toll could be independently verified.
The airstrikes are the latest clash between the two neighbors since cross-border tensions spiked earlier this year.

blocks.caption: Pakistan accuses Afghanistan of harboring militants, which Kabul deniesImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: What do we know about the latest Pakistani airstrikes on Afghanistan?

The Afghan government spokesman said three civilian homes in the southern province of Helmand and in the eastern province of Kunar, which borders Pakistan, were hit, killing nine and injuring 11 others.
Residents of Helmand told the AFP news agency that three bombs had struck their village, and there is "no military or anything else" in the area.
"We condemn this act and consider this an act of aggression and a crime that violates all universally accepted principles," Zabihullah Mujahid said.

blocks.caption: Men salvage their belongings from the debris of a house in Kunar provinceImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: Authorities in Islamabad, however, said that 22 militants had been killed, and that weapons and ammunition had been destroyed.
The airstrikes on militant hideouts were "well planned and calibrated" and were carried out "with precision and accuracy," Pakistan's Ministry of Information said.
"Maximum precautions were taken and it was ensured that no collateral damage occurs," the statement said.
What's behind the conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan?
The strikes overnight are the third time in the past two weeks that Pakistan has hit targets in Afghanistan.
Simmering tensions since the Taliban seized power in 2021 erupted into open conflict last year​​​​​​.
The two countries held peace talks in April to shore up a March truce, but sporadic flare-ups have continued in the months since.
Islamabad accuses the Taliban government in Kabul of harboring militants who carry out attacks across the border in Pakistan, an allegation Afghanistan denies.
"The threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan," Pakistan's information ministry said. "Our action precisely targeted the terrorist hubs."
Since the conflict escalated last year, Pakistan has closed its border crossings with Afghanistan, which is heavily reliant on foreign food and humanitarian aid.
Last week, the United Nations said more than 1,100 civilians had been killed or injured in Afghanistan as a result of the cross-border conflict this year.
Pakistan insists that it does not target civilians.
Are Pakistan and Afghanistan heading for war?

articles.title: Nature boys and girls – here’s your chance to get published in the Guardian
articles.summary:
Our wildlife series Young Country Diary is looking for articles written by children, about their autumn encounters with nature

Once again, the

blocks.text: Once again, the Young Country Diary series is open for submissions! Every three months we ask you to send us an article written by a child aged 8-14.
The article needs to be about a recent encounter they’ve had with nature – whether it’s a hedge full of berries, a beetle on the move, or a nervous deer.

It doesn’t matter if the child is a nature expert or not – we’re especially keen to reach teachers who might like to get their class outside and noticing nature. And note that any child who has their article published will be paid!
The deadline for autumn submissions is noon on Monday 2 November.

Four of the entries will be chosen to be published in the newspaper and online – two each in October and November. (Note that any early birds who submit a piece before the 15th stand a chance of being published in October.) If you don’t get selected this time, don’t worry, the form will reopen on 1 January for winter submissions, after it takes a break in December.

blocks.caption: Young Country Diary writer Aphra looking through her binoculars

blocks.text: How your child can take part
First of all, we’re looking for children age 8 to 14, so we will need your permission, as parent or guardian. Then here’s what the child needs to do:
Step 1 – Go out one day to where there is some nature. It could be their local woods or beach, their garden, a farm, or simply the nearest park.
Step 2 – Write an article of 200-250 words telling us what they saw and what happened.
Step 3 – Send the article to us using the form below. We ask that you fill in the form yourself rather than the child.

Photos/drawings – These are helpful (especially landscape rather than portrait) but they are not a condition of entry. If you have some, please tell us in the “more information” field, as there’s no way to attach them to the form.
Hints and tips for any budding YCD writers
If the child gets stuck and doesn’t know what to write about, here are a few pointers:
Good nature writing starts with the senses – so what did you see and hear? What about smell and touch? Take notes when you’re out and about so you don’t forget
How would you describe what happened? Did it remind you of anything?

It’s great to look up some extra information about what you saw, and tell us about that too. For example, if you find an interesting-looking bug, see if you can find out what type of butterfly it was, how long they live – any juicy details!
You can think big, and describe the whole scene – the sky, the horizon, the landscape. Or you can think small, and tell us some details about the butterfly’s wings or the beetle’s markings.
What did your encounter with nature make you think about? How did it make you feel?

blocks.caption: Young Country Diary writer Henry birdwatching on Dartmoor. Photograph: Family handout

blocks.text: Anyone can enter their child who is aged between 8 and 14 and based in the UK. You the parent/guardian will be contacted if your child’s piece is selected for publication, and you will be paid on behalf of the child.
For further inspiration, here are a few recent Young Country Diaries: Aled, 8, on his afternoon of crabbing Jess, 10, on the jellyfish party Henry, 14, on a weary wheatear
A note on AI usage

We’d love to hear what your child has to say, and how they’d like to say it. For that reason, we ask that every sentence is written by the child, not by LLMs such as ChatGPT or Claude. LLMs may be used for research, planning or checking, though their output should be used with caution and double-checked.
Many thanks, and good luck!
Paul, editor of Young Country Diary and Country Diary

We ask that the parent/guardian fills in the form below, rather than your child. Your responses are secure as the form is encrypted and only the Guardian has access to your contributions. One of our journalists will be in contact with you, as parent or guardian, before we publish, so please do leave contact details.

articles.title: Executive session? House’s budget amendment review panel livestream delayed for hours
articles.summary: It’s been four hours since the House of Representatives’ budget amendments review subcommittee meeting was supposed to start, but there was still no livestream as of 5 pm

blocks.text: LOWER CHAMBER. The House of Representatives Session Hall.
House of Representatives' Facebook page
It’s been four hours since the House of Representatives’ budget amendments review subcommittee meeting was supposed to start, but there was still no livestream as of 5 pm

items: The BARSC meeting on budget amendments was delayed multiple times, raising concerns about transparency in the allocation of public funds.
Critics, including members of the People's Budget Coalition, argue that the meeting is being conducted without proper public oversight and media access.
The creation of BARSC was intended to enhance transparency, but the public's long wait and lack of information suggest otherwise.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
In school, at work, or even in a meeting, there’s usually a grace period for people who arrive late.
But how long is the grace period when the meeting is supposed to discuss how billions in public funds will be allocated?
The House of Representatives’ budget amendments review subcommittee (BARSC) meeting was scheduled to start at 1 pm on Thursday, October 1.
The House’s YouTube page initially indicated that the livestream would begin at 1:30 pm.
At around 2:30 pm, the schedule was pushed back again to 3 pm.
As of 5 pm, however, the livestream had yet to start.
So, what’s going on?
People’s Budget Coalition co-convener and technical adviser AJ Montesa thinks there’s an “executive session” going on.

“Where is the space for the members of the HOR (House of Representatives) who want to participate in the debate? Why are the decisions and deliberations on how to allocate Filipino taxpayers’ money only in the hands of a few members of the Appro[priations] Committee, of which there will be no public record?” Montesa told Rappler.
“Nakakagalit,” he added. (Infuriating)
Rappler asked House appropriations committee chairperson Mika Suansing for clarification on the reason for the delay and the status of the BARSC meeting. There was no response as of writing.
People’s Budget Coalition national coordinator Mary Abigail Modales also criticized the proceedings.
“This BARSC is a farce. It is censored and curated to show what they want us to see,” Modales said.
Unlike regular budget hearings, members of the media are not allowed to cover BARSC meetings in person.
Montesa said the coalition had asked the House to allow media and civil society organizations to observe the proceedings in person.
But, he said, their request was ignored.

“Easy for them to pay lip service for transparency and openness, but then the end result is they’re essentially having a small committee and just using the BARSC as a way to publicize the finished negotiations,” Montesa said.
This is not the first time civil society groups have raised concerns about being sidelined from the House’s budget deliberations.

One of the small committee members was former congressman and now fugitive Zaldy Co, who has been at the center of allegations surrounding the national budget and the multibillion-peso flood control controversy.
The creation of the BARSC was supposed to bring greater transparency to the budget amendment process.
But on Thursday, the public was left waiting for hours just so they could watch the proceedings.
A grace period might be acceptable for a late class, meeting, or workday.
But this is the national budget. This is public money. And the public is watching. – Rappler.com

The House prosecution panel’s decision not to field former senator Antonio Trillanes IV as a witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte is a caution for the best, private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said.

“That is his [Trillanes'] decision. Congresswoman Luistro just communicated whatever his considerations are,” Kapunan told reporters, referring to House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas, who told the Senate impeachment court that the prosecution “finally decided” not to field Trillanes as witness for the prosecution.
Trillanes later said in a statement that it was he who asked the prosecutors to drop him from the witnesses' list.
“For me, I’m all for fight, fight, fight. [I] take no prisoners. That’s my attitude. But I guess there is wisdom in being cautious because the evidence is strong enough,” Kapunan added.

Kapunan said that the prosecution has been able to present evidence of the Vice President's failure to disclose certain assets in her SALN such as her links to Metro City Chow Foods Corporation as one of the member of the board of directors; the value of her guns; as well as the P6-million property in Matina, Davao City and P3-million property in Samal island acquired by her husband Manases Carpio which were not reflected in her joint SALN filing with her husband.

articles.title: House member cites 'cash management issues' for delayed project, aid releases
articles.summary: A member of the House of Representatives attributed the National Unity Party"s (NUP) complaint about delayed releases for infrastructure projects and social services to “cash management issues,”…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 5:08pm

A member of the House of Representatives attributed the National Unity Party’s (NUP) complaint about delayed releases for infrastructure projects and social services to “cash management issues,” rather than what the party described as the practice of punishing districts and communities for the opinions or votes of their representatives that run counter to majority positions.

In a press conference on Wednesday, House Deputy Speaker and NUP president Rep. Ronaldo Puno said, "When a congressman does not vote the way the majority wants us to vote, it is not the correct reaction to deprive their constituents, and their voters, and their communities of whatever assistance that they deserve. Ang bawian, kami na lang. Huwag na yung distrito." (Let the backlash fall on us, not on the district.)
"Sometimes you will talk to departments. I won't mention specific ones. They will say we cannot release this because there was an order to stop," he added.
Puno also stated that some members of other parties share this sentiment.

Quezon 1st district Rep. Mark Enverga, a member of the Nationalist People's Coalition and part of the majority bloc in the House of Representatives, confirmed that some fund releases are on hold, but he believes it may be tied to budget issues.

"We know maraming naka-hold. And we know na ‘yung budget, tight yung deficit issues. So siyempre, it’s cash management also," Enverga, who is a member of the Nationalist People's Coalition, said in an interview Thursday.
"May mga nakakausap kasi ako na 'yung mga hindi supposedly sumusunod. I asked them kung may release sila. Mayroon naman silang releases," he stated.
Enverga said the executive department could better explain the issue.

"Saka siguro ‘yung collections. It could be that. But of course that’s the executive. Sila naman ang familiar with that. It’s the DBM who would know better sa cash management position ng executive," he said.

Enverga's partymate Ilocos Sur 2nd district Rep. Kristine Singson-Meehan added that "even ‘yung mga nag-yes actually, nagfa-follow up sila sa amin, for those that said yes during that big issue about the impeachment voting. Parang it’s all the same. If something is not being implemented or something is being implemented, it’s for all. It’s happening in all districts."
Singson-Meehan stated that fund releases were "moving, but it’s slow."

"Plus, there was the fuel crisis na they prioritize lang ‘yong subsidies. So priority ‘yon. So whatever that’s usually being put down to everywhere, na-hold lang kasi they prioritize, which everyone agreed na mauna ‘yung mga ‘yon," she added.
The NUP also complained that even fund releases for 2025 were delayed.
Enverga explained it may be because of scrutiny of flood control projects.
"I think magulo ‘yon kasi na-FLR (For Later Release) talaga, questionable, ‘di ba? It’s 2025, maraming questionable yata. I don’t know how that’s treated," he said.
The NUP also said yesterday that "there's an uneven and selective approach in the programming and continuation of DPWH projects across certain districts and provinces."
But Enverga and Singson-Meehan disagreed.
"I don’t think so... We don’t see a pattern kasi," Singson-Meehan said.
"Hindi naman siguro because everyone gets a release... Especially those ‘yung mga who abstained or did not vote (in the impeachment,) may release sila, as far as I’ve spoken to them," Enverga said.
Enverga added that the NPC has not yet conducted a meeting on this issue.
When asked for his comment, House Minority Leader and 4Ps Party-list Rep. Marcelino Libanan replied, "Wala naman kaming ganoong problema sa minority." —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Boots owner ‘closing in on sale to Canada’s Weston family for $9bn’
articles.summary: Deal would mark return of Canadian family to UK after it sold Selfridges department store for £4bn in 2022

blocks.text: The private equity owner of high street pharmacy Boots is reportedly closing in on a deal to sell the business to the Canadian branch of the billionaire Weston family for $9bn (£7bn).

Sycamore Partners, which bought the wider Walgreens Boots Alliance for $23.7bn in 2025, is said to be in advanced talks with the Westons, with the Financial Times reporting that a deal could be completed as soon as next week.
If successful, it would mark the return of the Canadian branch of the Weston family to the UK high street, having previously owned Selfridges.
The family later sold the department store chain for £4bn in 2022. The Westons are widely known throughout Canada for owning the grocery store Loblaws and the pharmacy chain Shoppers Drug Mart.

The UK branch of the family, which operates its businesses through a separate investment vehicle, are known for holding a majority stake in Primark through the parent company Associated British Foods.

News of the prospective Weston deal comes months after Sycamore tried and failed to sell Boots to the Australian pharmaceutical group Sigma Healthcare in a deal that would have valued the business at $10bn this summer.

Sycamore has been widely expected to spin off and sell Boots – alongside other parts of the group – after its takeover of the Walgreen Boots Alliance last year. It as has already split the group into five stand-alone companies.

Boots, which was founded in Nottingham in 1849 by John Boot, has changed hands several times in the past 20 years. After a merger with Alliance Unichem in 2006, the combined company was taken over by the private equity firm KKR in 2007, before Walgreens first took a 45% stake in 2012 and then completed a takeover at the end of 2014.
Boots – which has 1,800 stores across the UK – employs about 51,000 people, including about 6,000 at its headquarters in Beeston, three miles south-west of Nottingham.

This summer it reported that revenues had risen 3.2% to £7.5bn in the year to the end of August 2025, with pre-tax profit up by 25% to £337m. It said strong demand for weight loss jabs and beauty products had helped increase its profits.
