articles.title: Overnight, Meta deleted all her accounts. AI customer service won’t let her reach a human
articles.summary: Toronto resident Jasmine Ault says Meta disabled her accounts overnight, without giving her a reason, and that she's been unable to get past their AI chatbots to speak to a human to resolve the…

image.caption: Jasmine Ault, a Toronto resident who used social media for marketing and as a personal scrapbook of her life, says her Meta accounts were deleted overnight, with no reasoning provided to her as to why. When she attempted to appeal, a wall of AI chatbots shut her down, a trend that is being seen acro

blocks.text: When she woke up in the middle of the night last Thursday, Jasmine Ault went to check her phone like she usually would.
But she didn’t expect to see a notification telling her that her Instagram and Facebook account had been permanently disabled by Meta.

It was only the start of an odyssey of frustration and anxiety spanning multiple days as Ault struggled to get to the bottom of how 20 years of personal data and professional contacts had been taken from her overnight — all while being stonewalled by AI customer service with no option to reach a human being, even after paying extra.

“It feels like I've lost everything in a metaphorical fire with my digital albums and my digital memories,” Ault, who lives in Toronto, told CBC News. “And who's going to protect those if I can only speak to AI?”

Ault is only the latest victim in a pattern growing increasingly common over the past two years. Numerous Canadians have reported their Meta accounts being abruptly wiped, leaving them stuck interfacing with AI chatbots unable to grasp the complexities of their situation.

One Canadian lost 18 years of data on Facebook after posting photos from a family trip, and had a second account banned when she tried to return. Others lost accounts vital to advertising their businesses. Many believe their accounts were incorrectly flagged by Meta’s AI moderation, and while some have had accounts restored after reaching out to media, others have never had them restored.
Meta has not responded to a request for comment from CBC News.
It comes at a time when companies are increasingly adopting AI in customer service, despite data showing customers aren’t on board.
Lack of empathy frustrating to customers

A global survey released earlier this year of more than 34,000 customers, service representatives and executives found that half of customers surveyed reported a lack of empathy as their biggest frustration with AI customer service.

And while 87 per cent of customers ranked phone calls as a preferred customer service channel, the survey found only seven per cent of executives plan to prioritize them. The research, commissioned by software company ServiceNow in partnership with research firm ThoughtLab, included 1,350 customers and 195 executives in Canada.

items: AI agents lag far behind human workers. Why are tech companies laying off the humans?
As more teens turn to AI for emotional support, experts say it's no substitute for human connection

blocks.text: Ela Veresiu, associate professor of marketing at the Schulich School of Business at York University, explained that companies are buying into AI en masse despite the backlash because of the promise of efficiency and lower costs.
“It is a lot cheaper to have an AI that responds to customer service queries than to hire people that can potentially respond, or be available to respond, 24/7,” she told CBC News.

But while an AI chatbot is able to direct customers to existing information, such as a business’s hours of operation, they can’t handle complex “why” questions, she said, and it can create huge problems.

If a company has competitors, customers frustrated with poor AI rollout can take their business elsewhere, potentially leading businesses to change strategies. But for singularly massive social media companies like Meta, which offer unique services, there’s no business incentive to change their policies.
“Customers may grumble and be dissatisfied by the overreliance of AI and customer service, but ultimately, they have no choice in the marketplace,” Veresiu explained.
‘It’s people’s lifelines’

Ault started her Facebook account in 2006, the first year it was public. After she received the news that her Instagram, Facebook and even a linked Instagram for her dog had all been deactivated, Ault says she stayed up for the next 26 hours straight, desperately trying to appeal the decision.
Screenshots she shared with CBC News stated that her accounts were disabled because her Facebook “doesn’t follow our rules,” but Ault said she was never told what rules her Facebook allegedly broke.

Ault believes her Facebook had been recently hacked, and that this may have caused her accounts to be flagged. But within minutes of pressing the appeal button, she was told her case was closed and she would not be permitted to appeal again, without giving her the opportunity to plead her case.

She created a backup Instagram account and paid for Meta Verification under the impression that it would allow her to reach a human support agent. Meta’s Verification program has various paid tiers with perks such as enhanced support. Standard, the option Ault went for, costs $14.99 US (roughly $21 Cdn).
But the enhanced support she received was simply another AI chatbot, which swiftly told her the ticket was being closed, and that she had reached her limit of support interactions.

items: Hamilton woman says cooking business erased 'from existence' after Instagram account shut down by Meta
'It's sheer panic': Ottawa restaurateur says Meta wrongly banned her business accounts
Meta suspended his business's social accounts — it took him a month to reach a human

blocks.text: CBC News has reached out to Meta, but the company has not responded to questions about Ault’s account and whether access to a human customer service agent — once a staple of all customer service interactions — is now only accessible at a high monthly cost. Of Meta’s verification tiers, only Premium and Max, which have a monthly fee of $150 US and $500 US respectively, mention the ability to “request a call from an agent.”

“It, to me, feels like Meta is trying to cut corners by not paying a human, when they're worth billions and billions of dollars,” Ault said. “And it feels almost sick to me that they just think, like, 'We can just shut these people's accounts down, they can't get through to us and talk to us,' and it's people's lifelines. It's people's memories. It's people's everything."
She added that since she used social media to provide marketing to clients for her side business, she’s now losing out on those financial opportunities and connections.

Jon Festinger, a lecturer at the Peter A. Allard School of Law at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, said Canadians may have legal recourse to challenge account deletion in court by arguing damages that demand a remedy, particularly if they used their social media for business purposes.
“It should be relatively easy to prove the damages, at least the reputational damage, and perhaps more,” he said.
Local restaurant faces setback after Meta wrongfully shut down their social media accounts

Canadian courts have made some steps toward dealing with AI chatbots — Air Canada was found liable for its chatbot’s hallucinated advice to a customer in 2024, for instance — but there are still gaps in Canadian consumer law when it comes to customer rights and AI, he said.
Regulation needed now, experts say
That’s where experts believe regulation should come in.

"Any technical solution makes mistakes," Shion Guha, an assistant professor at the University of Toronto and director of the Human-Centered Data Science Lab, told CBC News. "What it's really about is that people lack a way to get the mistake fixed."
Companies must be required to provide a clear pathway to a human agent and a fair appeals process, especially if automated systems are being used to moderate social media, he said.

items: Trump says top tech firms have signed accord to 'self-police' AI development
Is AI evolving too fast? A look at the debate on slowing it down

blocks.text: “Literally in every other facet of our life, if we are appealing ... a potentially unfair decision, we reach a human being,” he added, giving the example of speeding tickets and tax appeals.
“People expect that that will transpose to private social media platforms, and it doesn't because … they're not required to, because there's no regulatory framework in place for that.”

An existing model is the EU’s Digital Services Act, which was implemented in 2024 to update rules for online services, including guaranteeing transparency and a full appeal process when content is removed.
Instagram users blame Meta’s AI moderators for wrongful suspensions
New legislation around AI chatbots in Canada was introduced in June, but it focuses on increasing safety requirements to protect children online, not consumer rights.

CBC News has not yet received a response from AI Minister Evan Solomon’s office to questions on whether upcoming legislation will ensure Canadians have the right to access a human customer service agent during appeals processes.

In the meantime, Canadians like Ault have their digital footprints hanging in the balance, hoping that the thousands of photos, conversations and memories lost to their disabled accounts might one day be restored.

articles.title: Is this Quebec riding encroaching on Newfoundland and Labrador? Depends who you ask
articles.summary: Looking at Quebec’s electoral map, the riding of Duplessis, located in the province’s Côte-Nord region, might not stand out in the minds of the majority of Quebecers. But a closer look at the…

image.caption: A map appearing on the Élections Québec website shows the riding of Duplessis. The official border separating Quebec from the southern part of Labrador appears as a dotted line and labelled as non-definitive. (Élections Québec/Gouvernement du Québec)

blocks.text: Montreal·New

Looking at Quebec’s electoral map, the riding of Duplessis, located in the province’s Côte-Nord region, might not stand out in the minds of the majority of Quebecers. But a closer look at the district’s boundaries — as they appear on the Élections Québec’s electoral map — reveals a long-standing grievance held by Quebec.
Quebec has never recognized the 1927 land border between itself and Labrador
Looking at Quebec’s electoral map, the riding of Duplessis, located in the province’s Côte-Nord region, might not stand out in the minds of the majority of Quebecers.
While it ranks as the province’s second-largest riding in terms of sheer size, with a land area of 249,090.96 square kilometres, the region is sparsely populated.

According to Élections Québec, there are 37,073 people appearing on the electoral list, out of a population of just over 48,000, the majority of which are concentrated in the cities of Sept-Îles and Port-Cartier.
But a closer look at the district’s boundaries — as they appear on Élections Québec’s electoral map, at least — reveals a long-standing grievance held by Quebec.
That’s because the map, also used by the media, including CBC News, encompasses a swath of southern Labrador, showing it as being a part of Quebec.
Map shows portion of Labrador which is included in the Duplessis riding
In a statement to CBC News, Élections Québec spokesperson Gabriel Sauvé-Lesiège cited a historical dispute over a portion of the territory going back almost 100 years.
"In 1927, the Privy Council in London defined a land boundary between Quebec and Newfoundland and Labrador — a boundary that Quebec governments have never formally recognized," he said.
"This explains why any map of Quebec produced by a public institution includes this part of the territory."
The council had been asked to define Labrador’s coastal area to settle a dispute between Quebec, represented by Canada, and Newfoundland, which at the time was a Dominion of the British Empire.
The ruling favoured Labrador, placing the land border far inland to encompass the entire water basin of rivers flowing east into the Atlantic Ocean — including the Churchill Falls river system.
When Newfoundland joined Canada in 1949, this exact 1927 boundary was entrenched into the Canadian Constitution.

While Quebec government maps will include the boundary line, it often appears as a dotted line with a label saying it is either not definitive or not final, reflecting Quebec’s position that an injustice was committed.
What does the map mean for voters in the riding?
The issue of the riding map raises the question of who can vote in a Quebec provincial election.
Would a resident domiciled in Newfoundland and Labrador, but within the Duplessis riding’s limits, be eligible?
Élections Québec says that since the scenario is hypothetical, it can’t provide further details.
"Currently, no one living in this part of the territory is registered on Quebec’s permanent electoral list," Sauvé-Lesiège said.
"Should such a situation arise, a thorough analysis would be required."

According to Kathryn Furlong, a professor of geography at the University of Montreal, the inclusion of a portion of Labrador functions primarily as a political statement, rather than serving an active voting population.
"I think it is a constant, subtle message to people that this is something that belongs to the province of Quebec," she said.

The part of Labrador that's included in the riding of Duplessis is what Quebec defines as ultra petita, Furlong said — a Latin term for something that's granted in a legal decision above and beyond what was initially asked for.
The disputed territory, she explains, "was not requested by Newfoundland during the border decision of 1927, but accorded to Newfoundland as part of that decision."
PCs, Liberals slam ‘disrespectful’ Hydro-Quebec map suggesting Labrador border isn’t final
Border dispute as leverage
The area along the southern border of Labrador remains particularly coveted due to its hydroelectric potential.
It’s been a point of contention on both sides of the border for decades, as the line cuts through five major river systems flowing south into the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

Furlong said the border hasn't been a real barrier to Quebec development in hydroelectricity, especially in the case of Churchill Falls, where costs are concentrated on one side of the border, and wealth and benefits on the other.

items: Quebec-Labrador border is becoming political fodder

blocks.text: And because Labrador is geographically isolated, its resources typically have to pass through Quebec to reach the rest of Canada or the global market.

For Quebec, maintaining a policy of non-recognition — such as drawing a "non-definitive" border on provincial maps — has served as an ongoing tool for political and economic leverage, whether in terms of negotiating energy deals or stoking nationalism.
In June, the Parti Québécois published its Blue Book on sovereignty, a policy document describing an independent Quebec.

While the party acknowledges there's "no legal recourse" to challenging the border decision, it says an independent Quebec would submit a claim for redress, as part of its overall negotiations with Canada.
"For Quebec, the only way to redress this injustice would be to propose a political settlement, or even financial compensation," the document says in French.
For Furlong, who grew up in Labrador, the discourse surrounding the border and its mapping seems very aggressive.

“It feels that people who have by and large probably never set foot in Labrador and never will, claim a territory as theirs for the purposes of resource extraction, not for any kind of purpose of good governance."

items: Indigenous turnout remains low in Quebec amid calls for political inclusion

blocks.text: She says this is something that Newfoundland is also guilty of, and that Indigenous communities in Labrador often find themselves feeling squeezed between the interests of Newfoundland and Quebec.
While the border issue invariably surfaces around election time, Newfoundland and Labrador Premier Tony Wakeham reiterated that the "matter is not up for debate."

In a statement to CBC News, the premier’s office noted that the "borders of Newfoundland and Labrador are clear and recognized" and the "issue was settled a long time ago by a binding and legal decision."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Annabelle Olivier is a digital journalist at CBC Montreal. She previously worked at Global News as an online producer. You can reach her at anne.isabelle.olivier@cbc.ca.
With files from Ashley Fitzpatrick

articles.title: Australian couple on plane diverted after flydubai pilot’s alleged attack on co-pilot
articles.summary: Two people from Sydney were on board flight to Tel Aviv that was dramatically diverted to Saudi Arabia after one pilot allegedly stabbed the other

blocks.text: Two Australian citizens onboard a flight to Tel Aviv that was diverted after one of the pilots allegedly stabbed the other in an attack are “safe,” the foreign minister confirmed.
The passengers are a Jewish couple from Sydney, the Israeli embassy in Australia confirmed to the Guardian on Thursday.
No further details were provided.
The flydubai aircraft was travelling from the United Arab Emirates to Israel when it was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
In a post on social media, Penny Wong thanked the “heroes” for thwarting the attack.
“Relieved to confirm at least two Australians who were on the Flydubai flight to Israel are safe – thanks to the heroes who thwarted the attack and helped bring the passengers to safety,” she wrote.
“We’re thinking of those injured and hope for their full recovery.”
One of the pilots, whom Israeli officials said was an Omani citizen, is accused of stabbing his co-pilot. During the alleged attack, the plane plunged about 17,000 feet in just two minutes.

Passenger Yaniv Hayoun later recounted how he and other passengers heard screaming and felt pressure as the plane dived before forcing their way into the cockpit and finding the attacker at the instrument panel.

“I grabbed the attacker, put him in a chokehold, and dragged him out first,” Hayoun said during a meeting with Netanyahu after the plane had landed safely and the passengers were flown to Israel. “He was trying to destroy the instruments to disable the plane.”
Israel’s ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, said the incident reminded him of the 11 September attacks.
“You have here a very special incident, and due to the real heroism of some people on board, they were saved.”
Newman said heightened security alerts had been issued after the attack.
“It just shows that … those that hate Israel also hate the peace.
“It’s an attempt to hit at the peace itself, at the Abraham Accords, and the relationships which Israel does have with Arab and Muslim countries.”
The Abraham Accords normalised relations between the UAE and Israel in 2020.
Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said it was too early to tell who was ultimately behind the incident.
There are about 12,000 Australian citizens living in Israel and 25,000 in the UAE.

articles.title: Right time to question threshold rule before SC is after impeachment trial vote -Carpio
articles.summary: Retired Senior Associate Justice Antonio Carpio on Thursday agreed with the Supreme Court"s (SC) dismissal of the petitions challenging the ruling of the Senate impeachment court on the voting…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 3:47pm

Retired Senior Associate Justice Antonio Carpio on Thursday agreed with the Supreme Court’s (SC) dismissal of the petitions challenging the ruling of the Senate impeachment court on the voting threshold in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment.
In an interview on Super Radyo DZBB, Carpio said the petitioners should wait until an actual vote has occurred.

“Well, ang tamang panahon after the voting on guilt or acquittal. Kasi kapag may 16 votes to convict, so walang issue. "Today, speculative pa na magkaroon ng 16 votes o bababa ng 16, so ayaw ng Korte Suprema to decide on something that’s speculative,” Carpio said.

(Well, the proper time is after the voting on guilt or acquittal. Because if there are 16 votes to convict, then there is no issue. Today, it is still speculative that there will be 16 votes or that it will fall below 16, so the Supreme Court does not want to decide on something that is speculative.)
“Tama ‘yun, sangayon ako doon (that’s right, I agree with that),” he added.

On Wednesday, the SC dismissed the petitions filed by former Executive Secretary Vic Rodriguez, Berteni Causing, and lawyer Ernesto Francisco Jr. on procedural grounds, including lack of standing and prematurity.

They questioned the impeachment court’s ruling to base the two-thirds of the votes required for Duterte’s conviction on the number of senators who are capable of "legally and factually participating in the impeachment proceedings."
According to Carpio, the petitioners do not have legal standing as they are not directly affected by the issue.
He said that individuals who may have legal standing are Duterte or the senators.
Further, he explained that there would be no justiciable issue if 16 senators-judges voted.
“So intayin na lang natin. Kapag may 16, walang problema. Kapag below 16, doon magkakaproblema. Doon ide-decide,” he said.
(So let’s just wait for it. If there are 16 votes, there’s no problem. If it’s below 16, there will be a problem. The SC will decide then.)

Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero has explained that the senator-judges who are detained or suspended, who are sought by authorities whose whereabouts are unknown, who are suffering from a physical or medical incapacity, and who are beyond the coercive processes of the Senate will be excluded from the senator-judges who are qualified to vote. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Zimbabwe tycoon Wicknell Chivayo and wife killed in helicopter crash
articles.summary: Chivayo was known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to African presidents and lucrative government contracts.

blocks.text: Prominent Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife have been killed in a helicopter crash that left six people dead, his family have confirmed.
The helicopter came down in the Marondera rural area, about 70km (43 miles) east of the capital, Harare, on Wednesday evening. Police said all six people on board died.
Family spokesperson Herbert Chivayo confirmed the deaths of the businessman and his wife Lucy Muteke to state broadcaster ZBC, saying the family was devastated by the tragedy.
Chivayo was known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to some African presidents and lucrative government contracts that had repeatedly attracted scrutiny.
He had denied allegations of wrongdoing linked to his business dealings.

Police spokesperson Commissioner Paul Nyathi said the aircraft crashed at about 17:00 local time (15:00 GMT) and had six occupants, but authorities did not immediately identify all those on board. Two of the six were pilots, according to government officials.

ZBC reported that the group was travelling from Gandami in Chikomba, where Chivayo and his wife were building a rural home, when the helicopter crashed at Kudenga Farm about 40 minutes after take-off.
"We are at a loss for words after the tragic news," the family spokesperson, told the ZBC.
The cause of the crash was not immediately known, and police said investigations were under way. Emergency services were sent to the scene on Wednesday evening.
Earlier, government spokesman Nick Mangwana confirmed the crash, saying the helicopter was carrying "a prominent businessman, three other passengers and two pilots".
"Current information indicates that there were no survivors in this crash," Mangwana posted on X.
Chivayo was the managing director of Intratrek Zimbabwe and had built a high public profile through government contracts, philanthropy and displays of wealth on social media.

Among his best-known business ventures was a $172m (£128m) solar power project in Gwanda awarded to Intratrek by the state-owned Zimbabwe Power Company. The project became the subject of years of legal disputes.

He also came under scrutiny over the procurement of materials for Zimbabwe's disputed 2023 elections. Zimbabwe's anti-corruption commission investigated allegations surrounding contracts awarded to South African company Ren-Form but closed the inquiry in 2025, saying it had found no evidence linking Chivayo or the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission to wrongdoing.
Widely known as "Sir Wicknell", Chivayo frequently used the title publicly and on social media, although he was never given a British knighthood.
He was also known for giving away luxury cars and large sums of money to musicians, religious leaders and other public figures, often publicising the gifts on social media.
His connections extended beyond Zimbabwe.
Kenya's President William Ruto, who had previously appeared in public with Chivayo, paid tribute to him as a "dear friend" and sent condolences to the families of those killed.
"I will remember him for his friendship, his energy and his deep conviction in the possibilities of our continent," Ruto added.
Kenyan opposition figures had questioned Chivayo's repeated access to Ruto and State House.

He frequently publicised his access to African leaders, posting photographs of meetings with presidents including Zambia's Hakainde Hichilema, South Africa's Cyril Ramaphosa and Tanzania's Samia Suluhu Hassan, as well as Eswatini's King Mswati III.

articles.title: First home buyers with big loans among those most at risk of falling into negative equity, RBA warns
articles.summary: Central bank estimates fewer than one in 100 borrowers owe more on their home than its worth

blocks.text: The Reserve Bank says households are well placed to weather the twin storm of rising interest rates and falling property prices, although it says recent borrowers who have taken out big loans are most at risk of falling into negative equity.
Despite a deepening property price slump concentrated in Sydney and Melbourne, the RBA’s analysis suggested that fewer than one in 100 borrowers owe more on their home than it’s worth.

Those included first home buyers who took advantage of the government’s 5% home guarantee scheme, the RBA said, although evidence suggested that the share of these borrowers falling behind on their payments remained “contained”.

The RBA also estimated that even a 20% property price crash would only push about 5% of mortgages into negative equity – a testament to the fact most homeowners have enjoyed significant value gains over the years.
The RBA also found that most indebted homeowners were coping with higher borrowing costs and wages that were not keeping up with the recent burst of inflation.

The analysis showed a little under 2% of mortgaged homeowners didn’t have enough income to cover essentials and the mortgage payments, similar to six months earlier. That share would stay roughly the same “for some time”, based on the RBA’s forecasts, and well below the recent peak of nearly 5% in 2024.

“While some households continue to experience hardship, the estimated share of mortgagors in severe financial stress or in arrears has, so far, remained low, supported by the strong labour market and mortgagors’ savings and equity buffers,” the report said.
“Negative equity is insufficient to trigger default if borrowers remain able to service their loans, which remains the case for the vast majority of these households.”
The central bank’s latest financial stability review – a biannual assessment of the financial system – said the “threats to global financial stability continue to mount”.
after newsletter promotion
The governor of the RBA, Michele Bullock, last month said AI could be a bubble, and that “all central banks are a little bit worried about that”.
This concern was reiterated in the financial stability review, which said high valuations in global corporate debt and share markets meant they were vulnerable to a “disorderly” correction.

“One possible trigger could be a shift in sentiment towards the AI investment boom, which is increasingly fuelled by expectations of sustained rapid earnings growth and a debt-financing cycle that is becoming more opaque and circular,” the report said.
“Australia is unlikely to be immune” from the impact, it said.

Alongside the huge sums being invested in artificial intelligence, two ongoing conflicts – in the Middle East and Ukraine – alongside “intensifying strategic competition among major powers” underscored these threats, the RBA said.
The RBA also warned of the rising risk of cyber-attacks, potentially facilitated by AI, and a sudden sell-off in global bond markets.
“These external factors are the most prominent threats to financial stability in Australia.”

articles.title: ‘Where illegal ebikes go to die’: first bikes seized under new laws in NSW crushed
articles.summary:
Major Sydney hospital also warns recent injuries from ebikes include fractures, internal bleeding, as well as ‘perforation of certain organs’

  • Get our

blocks.text: The first illegal ebikes seized under new laws have been crushed in New South Wales, as a major Sydney hospital has warned of a spike in trauma injuries driven by those riding under the influence.

The NSW government crushed 23 ebikes at a wrecking yard in western Sydney on Thursday, turning them into scrap metal. NSW police are assessing applications for the return of an additional 13 bikes seized during a joint operation with Transport for NSW in the northern beaches in September.
The NSW transport minister, John Graham, told reporters onsite on Thursday “this isn’t a scene from Mad Max. This is where illegal ebikes go to die.”
Graham said tough new laws were necessary “because of some of the bad behaviour we’ve seen … on our state’s streets, on the golf courses in Sydney suburbs, even on the Sydney Harbour Bridge”.

On the same day, St Vincent’s hospital released figures that showed a 22% spike in legal and illegal ebike injuries, with 42% of those injuries triggering a trauma response and the majority being injured while riding under the influence of alcohol or drugs, riding too fast or without a helmet.
It found 361 patients presented to the hospital for ebike injuries between January and July, compared with 296 presentations during the same period last year.

Dr Ed Lewis, acting head of rehabilitation medicine, told reporters injuries included fractures, internal bleeding, as well as the “perforation of certain organs”. He said they often included brain injuries from severe head trauma, “as well as milder knocks, like a concussion, which can still have long-term repercussions for patients”.
Lewis told Guardian Australia that those contemplating riding an ebike home while intoxicated “need to have a plan B or a backup solution”.
after newsletter promotion
“The message that we want to say to people is: enjoy using ebikes, but respect what they are. Respect that they are fast. Wear a helmet and just don’t ride impaired.”
Graham said the government was concerned by the number of injuries, but it was “important to keep it in context”.
“The number of ebike injuries is still low compared to cars … but is rising,” he said. “If you’re not wearing a helmet, you are dicing with danger.”

He stepped aside to allow a giant metal claw pick up a tangle of ebikes, cracking frames in half and popping tyres. They were loaded into a conveyor belt before being crushed and shredded. Graham said batteries had been removed for safe disposal and recycling beforehand.

Under powers which came into effect in August, police and transport officers can seize bikes not restricted to 25km/h, whose maximum speed while not pedalling does not exceed 6km/h, and maximum continuous power of 500 watts, due to reduce to 250 watts in March 2029.

The government says the bikes crushed include one capable of speeds of more than 90km/h seized from a 14-year-old, a food delivery bike, and bikes with speed restriction settings that had been tampered with.

The 36 ebikes seized so far represent a fraction of the estimated 760,000 in the state. The changes were prompted by a surge in injuries and high-profile incidents, including one in which about 40 ebikes swarmed the Sydney Harbour Bridge in February. An expert review on implementing an age limit of between 12 and 16 was due to report back to the government in June.
The NSW premier, Chris Minns, appearing on the debut of Kyle Sandilands Live in August, said the government was “examining an … age limit of 12”, but hadn’t finalised the details.
On Tuesday, Graham would not say if the premier had revealed the planned age limit. “I want to discuss this with my colleagues and also with the public,” he said.

articles.title: Tennessee halts woman's execution after 'failed' attempt
articles.summary: Christa Pike was found alive and snoring, despite being administered two injections of a lethal drug. The state governor has ordered a review of the botched execution.

image.caption: Christa Pike was just 18 when convicted of murder in 1995 [FILE: December, 2007]Image: J. Miles Cary/Knoxville News Sentinel/USA TODAY NETWORK/REUTERS

blocks.text: The governor of Tennessee ordered a halt to the execution of Christa Gail Pike, convicted of murdering a schoolmate more than 30 years ago, after authorities "failed" to carry out her execution on Wednesday.
Despite being administered two doses of a lethal drug, Pike was found breathing.
The execution had been scheduled for 11:00 a.m. local time at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution. The injections were administered in front of witnesses, including journalists.
Pike, 50, was alive and loudly snoring after the attempted lethal injection and was taken to a hospital in an ambulance, her attorneys said.
She received treatment at the hospital, but authorities had not yet informed them about her condition, her attorneys added.

blocks.caption: Pike was heard gasping after the injection and taken for medical treatmentImage: George Walker IV/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: What do we know about the execution attempt?
Pike would have been the first woman executed in the southern US state of Tennessee in over 200 years.
According to media witnesses, who were observing from a separate room, Pike was strapped to a gurney.
"I'm going to leave this world the way I spent most of my life, and that is in love," she said in her "last" words.
By 8:26 p.m., witnesses reported that the second dose of pentobarbital had been given to Pike.
However, Pike was heard snoring behind the closed curtain until the microphone was cut off at 8:53 p.m.
At that time, media witnesses were asked to leave the room.
Tennessee orders investigation into failed execution of Christa Gail Pike
Governor Bill Lee said in a statement that he has ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred" and that scheduled executions will not be carried out this year.

"Carrying out a lawfully imposed sentence is among the State's most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective," he said.
Pike's attorney filed an emergency motion late Wednesday with the Tennessee Supreme Court seeking to immediately halt and stay the execution.
In their appeal, they said she was in "unnecessary agony" and that it was violating her right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment.
This is the second time an execution has failed in Tennessee this year. In May, Tony Carruthers' execution by lethal injection failed.
Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend committed the murder she was convicted for.
"I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I'd done," Pike had said in an earlier statement.

articles.title: Indonesia said they will respect Marcos decision on Mary Jane Veloso -- DOJ
articles.summary: Justice Undersecretary Deo Marco said Thursday that Indonesia has already stated that it will respect the decision of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Mary Jane Veloso when she returned…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 2:45pm

Justice Undersecretary Deo Marco said Thursday that Indonesia has already stated that it will respect the decision of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Mary Jane Veloso when she returned to the Philippines in 2024 after being detained there for years.
“Sinabi na ng Indonesia na kung anuman ang pasya ng Presidente ay gagalangin nila,” Marco said in a press briefing.
(Indonesia has said that they will respect the President’s decision.)
Last week, Marcos granted absolute pardon to Veloso, paving the way for her release from Philippine prison after languishing on death row in Indonesia over drug charges
Marco also cited a report of a news agency in Indonesia that stated that the Indonesian government is aware and respects the Philippines’ decision.
Meanwhile, Justice Undersecretary Nicholas Ty cited the agreement between the two countries.

Ty said the agreement stated that the “continued enforcement of the sentence of Mary Jane in the Philippines shall be governed by the laws and procedures of the Philippines, including the authority to grant permission, amnesty, or any other form of clemency.”

“Maliwanag sa kasunduan na nung nalipat na si Mary Jane dito sa bansa natin, pasya na ng Pilipinas kung anong mangyayari kay Mary Jane, ‘yung sa pagsilbi ng kanyang sentensya, at kung mabibigyan man siya ng kahit anong executive clemency,” he said.

(It was clear in the agreement that when Mary Jane was brought back to the country, it is up to the Philippine government on what will happen to her, her serving the sentence, and if she will be granted any executive clemency.)
Meanwhile, Ty also cited the non-punishment principle in the country’s human trafficking law in pushing for Veloso’s freedom.
“Ang mga biktima ng trafficking tulad ni Mary Jane ay dapat hindi panagutin ng kriminal doon sa mga bagay na nagawa nila, kahit illegal ito, bilang isang human trafficking victim,” Ty said.
(Victims of trafficking like Mary Jane should not be held criminally liable for the things they did, even if they are illegal, as a human trafficking victim.)
“In other words, kung may mga bagay na pinilit sa kanila or nalinlang sila para gawin, tulad ng pagbitbit ng droga tulad ng nangyari kay Mary Jane, dapat hindi panagutin ito,” he added.
(In other words, if there are things that they were forced or deceived into doing, such as carrying drugs as happened to Mary Jane, they should not be held liable for this.)
Ty said that the non-punishment principle is observed by other countries in Asia.
However, he said that the application is not that simple.

“Kaya doon talaga pumasok lahat ng mga negosyasyon natin, no? Kaya bakit 2015 pa lang kailangan natin mapakita sa Government of Indonesia na may human trafficking case talaga dito sa Pilipinas, may mga naaresto tayong trafficker, at kailangan ang testimony ni Mary Jane sa kasong iyon,” he said.

(That is why all our negotiations really came into play there, right? That is why as early as 2015, we needed to show the Government of Indonesia that there really was a human trafficking case here in the Philippines, that we had traffickers arrested, and that we needed Mary Jane’s testimony in that case.) —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: [DECODED] No, this ‘handsome’ Duterte grandson is not real
articles.summary: A young Duterte is racking up swooning comments and supporters online. Except he's synthetic.

blocks.text: A young Duterte is racking up swooning comments and supporters online. Except he's synthetic.

items: Lance Duterte, a purported son of Vice President Sara Duterte, is revealed to be a fabricated persona created using AI-generated images, despite gaining a significant following on social media.
Visual inconsistencies in his photos, confirmed by AI detection tools, indicate that the images are not real, and there is no official record of his existence.
The account has been used to promote pro-Duterte propaganda and manipulate public perception, particularly during critical political events involving the Duterte family.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Sharp features, styled hair, and easy confidence in front of a camera. At first glance, Lance is your stereotypical content creator. Adding to the charm is his surname: Duterte.
Lance Duterte is supposedly the son of Vice President Sara Duterte and grandson of former president Rodrigo Duterte. This has helped him rack up thousands of swooning comments and online supporters.

And in true Duterte fashion, he is often seen posing with a fist bump for photos at different locations — like Luneta Park and Davao City Hall. If that’s not enough proof of his lineage, he has also been posting photos with his supposed family, like his “aunt” Kitty and mother Sara.
There’s one problem with this almost-too-perfect image: he is not real.
Lance established his identity through his Facebook profile, “Lance Duterte (Official Account),” with over 382,000 followers on Facebook.

blocks.caption: DIGITAL IDENTITY. The Facebook profile of Lance Duterte. Rappler screenshot

blocks.text: He recently caught the public’s eye when he shared his photos posing in Luneta Park.

blocks.caption: HARD LAUNCH. A Facebook post by Lance Duterte showing photos of him in Luneta Park. Rappler screenshot

blocks.text: But a closer look at the images exhibits visual signs that they are AI-generated, such as jumbled letters at the Rizal Monument, the absence of the Torre Manila condo behind the monument, and an inaccurate shadow of Lance.

blocks.caption: VISUAL INCONSISTENCIES. A photo of Lance Duterte in front of the Rizal Monument shows telltale signs that it was AI-generated. Photo from the “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” Facebook page, graphics added by Rappler

blocks.text: ​AI image detection tools Hive Detect and Sightengine rated the image as 99.9% likely to be AI-generated, while ZeroGPT and DeepAI gave it a 91% AI-likelihood score.

​Lance also posted photos of him posing warmly with the Vice President and her husband, Manases “Mans” Carpio, and another set of pictures with Veronica “Kitty” Duterte and Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte. The same AI image detection tools said the pictures were AI-generated, but they were not labelled as AI content on Facebook.

blocks.caption: FAMILY PHOTOS. Screenshots of Facebook posts by Lance Duterte with pictures of him with members of the Duterte family. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Supporters of the Duterte family also reposted photos of Lance, echoing the narrative that he is related to the Duterte family.

blocks.caption: ONLINE DEBUT. Screenshots of Facebook posts from other pages about Lance Duterte. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: But in reality, it is publicly known that Vice President Duterte and Carpio only have three children: Mikhaila Maria (Sharky), Mateo Lucas (Stingray), and Marko Digong (Stonefish).
No official public record acknowledges his existence. His persona relies entirely on artificial intelligence to fabricate a person that does not exist.

Lance Duterte is the latest addition to the AI-generated media surrounding the Dutertes. Rappler has previously debunked AI-generated images and videos designed to draw sympathy and political support for the Duterte family.

blocks.caption: [DECODED] What makes AI-generated Duterte statues so popular online?

blocks.text: These synthetic contents are circulating amid critical political events for the Dutertes: the impeachment trial of Vice President Duterte and the continued detention of former president Duterte at The Hague, Netherlands, as he awaits his trial in the ICC.

blocks.caption: DUTERTE-CARPIO FAMILY. A screenshot of Vice President Sara Duterte posing for a family photo with her three children: Sharky, Stingray, and Stonefish, during her inauguration in Davao City on June 19, 2022. Rappler screenshot from the Inday Sara Duterte YouTube channel

blocks.text: Lance Duterte’s Facebook profile was created on September 26, 2021, serving as an alternative profile for another account named “Lance Kurt Duterte.”

blocks.caption: PROFILE HISTORY. A screenshot of the transparency information of the “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” profile from Facebook. Rappler screenshot

blocks.text: Facebook disabled the latter account on January 27, 2025, after a series of suspensions from 2022 until 2024.

blocks.caption: MULTIPLE STRIKES. Screenshots of posts by Lance Duterte stating that his “Lance Kurt Duterte” account was suspended and eventually disabled by Facebook. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: The “Lance Kurt Duterte” account featured a different face in its profile picture compared to the Lance Duterte persona circulating today.

blocks.caption: DIFFERENT FEATURES. A visual comparison of the profile photo of “Lance Kurt Duterte” in 2024 and an image of “Lance Duterte” today shows no resemblance. Photos from the “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” Facebook page

blocks.text: Rappler earlier fact-checked a claim in 2020 made by an account named “Lance Kurt Dong Duterte” that accused Tricia Robredo, daughter of then-vice president Leni Robredo, of allegedly sending hate messages to him. The account similarly claimed that he is the grandson of former president Duterte. Both of the Robredos have denied that the exchanges happened, and the account later became unavailable on Facebook.

blocks.caption: FALSE: Tricia Robredo sends hate messages to Duterte’s grandson

blocks.text: The “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” Facebook profile became active during the national campaign of Vice President Duterte and President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. in 2022. It became inactive in 2023, then posted about the Duterte family and the arrest of their ally, Pastor Apollo Quiboloy, in 2024.

blocks.caption: TIDES TURNED. Screenshots of posts by Lance Duterte from 2022 to 2024, indicating a tone shift in commentaries about President Marcos Jr. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: It became active again in 2025 to support Vice President Duterte and direct online attacks toward the Marcos Jr. administration, specifically after the arrest of former president Duterte over his crimes against humanity case in the International Criminal Court (ICC).

blocks.caption: DEFENDING THE DUTERTES. Screenshots of posts published by Lance Duterte after the arrest of former president Duterte in 2025. Rappler screenshots
[DECODED] How online supporters made a victim of Duterte after ICC arrest

blocks.text: In 2026, the account consistently promoted pro-Duterte propaganda. It recently responded to veteran news anchor Korina Sanchez’s remarks that Davao City “looks left behind,” and posted Davao City infrastructure updates paired with pro-Duterte hashtags.

blocks.caption: PRO-DAVAO PROPAGANDA. Screenshots of Facebook posts by “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” criticizing veteran anchor Korina Sanchez. Screenshots by Rappler

blocks.text: It also intensified its activity by humanizing the Lance Duterte persona with AI-generated content, attracting thousands of engagements from social media users. Posts about Lance have garnered comments from supporters, saying that he is ”handsome” and “soon to be an artist or politician.”

blocks.caption: LANCE’S FANS. Screenshots of comments from various Facebook posts about Lance Duterte. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Lance’s online fame has even extended beyond his own Facebook accounts. ​A fan-run Facebook page created on September 26, 2026 now has more than 3,800 followers as of writing. The page actively posts AI-generated videos of Lance, which have amassed thousands of reactions each.

blocks.caption: FAN PAGE. Screenshots of AI-generated videos of Lance Duterte posted by a Facebook page dedicated to him. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: The Global Risks Report 2026 by the World Economic Forum identified misinformation and disinformation as one of the most crucial global concerns, emphasizing that it is now facilitated by AI. The United Nations’ Independent International Scientific Panel on AI has also said in its preliminary report that AI-driven disinformation weakens the information ecosystem and disrupts democracy. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Veloso to recruiters: Admit my innocence, let truth prevail
articles.summary: Mary Jane Veloso urged her recruiters to publicly admit that she had no part in the drug-smuggling crime that led to her nearly 15-year detention in Indonesia.

blocks.text: Mary Jane Veloso and her family attend a press briefing with Department of Justice officials on Oct. 1, 2026.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui
MANILA, Philippines — Mary Jane Veloso urged her recruiters to publicly admit that she had no part in the drug-smuggling crime that led to her nearly 15-year detention in Indonesia.
In a press conference at the Department of Justice on Thursday, October 1, Veloso said that she has always held two primary wishes: to be reunited with her family and to have her name cleared.
While both milestones have now been realized following the pardon granted to her, she expressed that she still hopes the admission of her innocence will come directly from the recruiters themselves.
"Siguro po ang mensahe ko lang sa kanila na sana ay manggaling po sa kanila mismo na wala akong kasalanan. Kasi importante po kasi 'yun eh," Veloso said.
(Perhaps my only message to them is that I hope it comes directly from them that I am innocent — because that is what truly matters.)

When asked what she plans to do, Veloso said that, despite returning to a private life, she remains committed to inspiring others by using social media from home to offer support and warn fellow Filipinos against illegal recruitment so they avoid the same ordeal.

"Ang plano ko po talaga syempre po babalik po sa buhay na kasama ang pamilya ko pero hindi ko pa rin po pinuputol yung magiging inspirasyon po nila ako para po hindi po sila matulad sa akin kasi marami naman pong paraan para gawin po yun," Veloso said.
(My plan is, of course, to return to life with my family, but I still don't want to stop being an inspiration to others so that they won't end up like me — after all, there are many ways to do that.)
She also said that she wanted to finish her education using the help from the government that she received.
Veloso's ordeal began in April 2010 when she was recruited by her neighbors in Talavera, Nueva Ecija, who promised her employment as a domestic helper in Malaysia.
Upon her arrival in Malaysia, she was told the job was no longer available and was instead sent to Indonesia for a holiday.
On April 25, 2010, she was arrested at the international airport in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, after authorities discovered 2.6 kilograms of heroin concealed inside her luggage.
Veloso consistently maintained that she was completely unaware of the drugs and had been deceived by her recruiters.

While Veloso was sentenced to death in Indonesia in October 2010, she was granted an indefinite reprieve in April 2015, just hours before her scheduled execution, to allow her to provide vital testimony against her recruiters.

The criminal complaints she filed for qualified trafficking in persons, illegal recruitment, and estafa against her recruiters are currently pending and being heard by Branch 89 of the Regional Trial Court in Nueva Ecija.
After nearly 15 years in Indonesian custody, Veloso was transferred back to the Philippines on Dec. 18, 2024.

articles.title: Philippines stands firm on arbitral victory as China rejects ruling at United Nations
articles.summary: The Philippines reiterated before the United Nations (UN) General Assembly that the 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated China's sweeping claims over the South China Sea is binding and should be…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 2:18pm

NEW YORK — The Philippines reiterated before the United Nations (UN) General Assembly that the 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated China's sweeping claims over the South China Sea is binding and should be respected by all parties.

The Philippine delegation pushed back against remarks issued by China, which insisted that the UN was not the appropriate forum to discuss South China Sea issues, aside from other assertions challenging the ruling.

Paolo Mapula, Second Secretary and First Committee Expert of the Permanent Mission of the Republic of the Philippines to the United Nations, conveyed the Philippines' position that stood pat on its sovereign rights over its exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

Exercising the Philippines' right of reply before the UN General Assembly, Mapula said, "This year marks the tenth anniversary of the Award. The Philippines recalls that UNCLOS and the Award are the twin anchors of our policy and actions in the South China Sea. UNCLOS establishes the legal framework within which all activities in the oceans and seas must be carried out. The Award, rendered by an Arbitral Tribunal constituted under Annex VII of UNCLOS, is final and binding upon the parties pursuant to Article 296 of the Convention and Article 11 of Annex VII."

The Philippines maintained that China's so-called nine-dash line claims in the South China Sea are "contrary to the Convention" and "exceed the geographic and substantive limits" of China's entitlements under the UNCLOS.

"The Tribunal further upheld the Philippines’ sovereign rights in its exclusive economic zone and found that certain actions therein violated those rights. These propositions are at the core of the Philippines' longstanding position on the Award," Mapula said.
Ayungin Shoal, Bajo de Masinloc

The Philippines' right of reply also cited a September 24 incident wherein China Coast Guard and Chinese militia vessels "interfered" with a rotation and resupply mission to the BRP Sierra Madre in Ayungin Shoal, which is within Manila's EEZ.
"Interference with lawful Philippine activities there must therefore be considered against the rights and obligations established by UNCLOS and clarified by the Award," he added.
Mapula likewise conveyed that the Philippines rejects China's establishment of a nature reserve at Bajo de Masinloc, also known as Scarborough Shoal, which also within Manila's territory.

"Here is a clear case where environmental protection cannot be invoked as a basis for measures inconsistent with these rights and with the applicable rules of international law. The Philippines rejects China's measure and calls for compliance with UNCLOS and the Award," Mapula said.
Call for respect

Saying the matter was an interest shared by the international community, the Philippines called on China to respect international law and comply with UNCLOS and the final and binding 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award.

"Mr. President, the Philippines reiterates that the Award did not create rights for the Philippines beyond those provided by UNCLOS. It authoritatively applied the Convention to the disputes submitted to the Tribunal. To respect the Award is therefore to respect UNCLOS and the integrity of the legal order established by the Convention," Mapula said.

"The Philippines will continue to exercise its rights and discharge its obligations in accordance with international law. We call on China to do the same and to comply with UNCLOS and the final and binding 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award," he added.
A decade after
For its part, China dismissed the Philippines' "erroneous claims."
China's Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Sun Lei, reiterated that China neither accepts nor recognizes the ruling.
"the Philippines' attempt to emphasize the fact that a decade has passed since the so-called award is 'utterly meaningless,'" Sun Lei said.

China argued that the ruling has failed to resolve maritime disputes between China and the Philippines and has instead contributed to growing regional tensions and strained relations between the two countries. — Dave Llavanes Jr./ VDV, GMA News

articles.summary: SILG Remulla open to dialogue with TBS

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 2:14pm
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Thursday said he is open to a dialogue with the True Brown Style (TBS) but the group must express commitment to stop its alleged criminal activities.
“Of course, but a dialogue must come with a commitment to stopping their nefarious activities,” Remulla said in an ambush interview.
Remulla made the statement after TBS Worldwide and other chapters defended their group, calling authorities to not generalize its members as criminals.
But Remulla said charitable activities do not erase alleged wrongdoing,
“That's their version of the truth. But we have our version. You know what they're doing? Alam niyo yung cosmetic, it doesn't hide the truth,” he said.

“They are really behind a lot of the sa mga kalokohan ng mga kabataan ngayon (illegal activities involving minors). We appreciate what they're doing but we're still not stopping, it's not stopping us from getting them,” he added.
Remulla said authorities already have a list of involved TBS members.

In a statement, TBS Worldwide said, “HUWAG LAHATIN. Hindi lahat ng may TBS sa pangalan, kulay, o affiliation ay kriminal. Hindi lahat ng TBS members pare-pareho ang ginagawa,” TBS Worldwide said in a Facebook post.
(DO NOT GENERALIZE. Not everyone with TBS in their name, color, or affiliation is a criminal. Not all TBS members do the same thing.)
“Marami sa amin ay professionals, workers, parents, business owners, at ordinaryong mamamayang sumusunod sa batas,” it added.
(Many of us are professionals, workers, parents, business owners, and ordinary law-abiding citizens.)
According to the group, some TBS members even help their communities and support people in need.
The group called on authorities to hold accountable those who commit crimes, while ensuring that allegations are backed by evidence and involved persons are given due process.
Remulla on Wednesday said members of the community-based criminal gang TBS have established a presence in all local government units (LGUs) in Metro Manila and in 78 provinces.
He described cases involving TBS as extremely alarming that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ordered authorities to dismantle the organization.

According to authorities, the group is composed largely of members in their late teens and early 20s and also recruits children as young as 14 to 15 years old and grooms them for criminal activities. Initiation rites for new members may include robbing convenience stores at gunpoint. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: 'Non-punishment' principles applied to Mary Jane Veloso — DOJ
articles.summary: The "non-punishment principle" for victims of human trafficking has been applied to Mary Joy Veloso.

blocks.text: Mary Jane Veloso sheds tears as she speaks during a press conference inside a school campus in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 26, 2026, a day after she was released from the correctional institution for women after authorities granted her pardon.
AFP / Ted Aljibe
MANILA, Philippines — The "non-punishment principle" for victims of human trafficking has been applied to Mary Joy Veloso.

In a press conference on Thursday, October 1, Justice Undersecretary Nicholas Ty said that the non-punishment principle in the country's anti-trafficking law has been applied to Veloso as a victim of human trafficking.

In the case of Veloso, this principle directly addresses her 2010 arrest for carrying 2.6 kilograms of heroin concealed in her luggage — an act she consistently maintained she was unaware of, having been deceived by her recruiters.

"Doon sa non-punishment principle ang mga biktima ng human trafficking tulad ni Mary Jane ay dapat hindi panagutin ng criminal sa mga bagay na nagawa nila kahit ilegal mga ito bilang isang human trafficking victim," Ty said.
(Under the non-punishment principle, victims of human trafficking like Mary Jane should not be held criminally liable for illegal acts they committed as a direct result of being trafficked.)

Under Section 17 of the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012, "trafficked persons" are to be recognized as victims and "shall not be penalized for unlawful acts committed as a direct result of, or as an incident or in relation to, being trafficked based on the acts of trafficking enumerated" in the law.
It also protects the victims from acts of "obedience to the order made by the trafficker."

However, Ty warned Filipinos not to let Veloso's case encourage them or give them a false sense of confidence to be deceived abroad under the assumption that they will automatically be saved as human trafficking victims.
He emphasized that Veloso went through an immense struggle and that bringing her home and securing a pardon was a highly difficult process.
"'Wag nating kalimutan bago tayo umabot sa araw na 'to napakaraming pinagdaanan ni Mary Jane. At hindi hindi din ganun kadali. Hindi din ganun kadali na mapauwi siya at ma-pardon siya," Ty said.
(Let us not forget that before reaching this day, Mary Jane went through so much. And it was by no means easy. Bringing her home and securing a pardon for her was far from easy as well.)

After more than a year in a Philippine prison without charges, Mary Jane Veloso, who was previously put on death row in Indonesia, is already free after being pardoned by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in September.
Her recruiters, meanwhile, are currently facing charges of human trafficking, large-scale illegal recruitment and estafa before a Nueva Ecija court.

articles.title: Can child support depend on seeing your child? Here’s what the law says
articles.summary: Patrick Garcia’s remarks raise a legal question. Here’s what Philippine law says.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Actor Patrick Garcia’s admission that he last provided financial support for his son with actress Jennylyn Mercado in 2017 has put child support obligations under the spotlight.
Garcia said he stopped giving financial support because he was no longer seeing his son, Alex Jazz, whom he shares with Mercado.
He made the admission in an interview with Ogie Diaz uploaded on YouTube on September 29, nearly 18 years after he and Mercado separated while she was pregnant with their son.
Garcia said he last saw Jazz in December 2017 and that he also last gave financial support that year.
“Hindi ko nakikita e, paano ko ibibigay?” Garcia said when asked why he stopped providing financial support.
He acknowledged, however, that he had been inconsistent with providing money and spending time with his son, saying he should have done better.
But does not contact remove a parent's obligation to provide support?
What does child support cover?
The Family Code requires parents to support their children, whether legitimate or illegitimate.

Article 195 of the Family Code lists “parents and their legitimate children and the legitimate and illegitimate children of the latter” and “parents and their illegitimate children and the legitimate and illegitimate children of the latter” among those who are legally obliged to support each other.
Support is not limited to food.

Under Article 194, “Support comprises everything indispensable for sustenance, dwelling, clothing, medical attendance, education and transportation, in keeping with the financial capacity of the family.”
The provision also states that education may include “schooling or training for some profession, trade or vocation, even beyond the age of majority.”
Is there a fixed amount?
The law does not prescribe a specific peso amount or percentage of a parent’s income that must be given as child support.
Article 201 provides that “the amount of support” shall be “in proportion to the resources or means of the giver and to the necessities of the recipient.”
The amount therefore depends on the child’s needs and the parent’s capacity to provide.

It may also be adjusted. Article 202 states that support “shall be reduced or increased proportionately,” depending on changes in the recipient’s needs and the resources or means of the person obliged to provide it.
When can support be demanded?
Article 203 provides that the obligation to give support is demandable from the time the person entitled to receive it needs it for maintenance.
However, the law states that support “shall not be paid except from the date of judicial or extra-judicial demand.”
This means the timing of a demand for support can have legal implications in determining when the obligation becomes enforceable.
What if a parent stops providing support?
A parent seeking support for a child may ask the courts to require the other parent to provide it.
In certain circumstances, failure to provide financial support may also be covered by Republic Act 9262, or the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act.
The law recognizes economic abuse, including acts that make or attempt to make a woman or her child financially dependent.
Still, failure to provide financial support does not automatically constitute a criminal offense under RA 9262. The circumstances of the case and the requirements of the law must be established.
The Supreme Court has also ruled that paternity must first be established before a person can be convicted under RA 9262 for economic abuse involving a child whose paternity he disputes.
Does marriage matter?
The Family Code expressly requires parents to support both legitimate and illegitimate children.
This means the obligation to support a child does not disappear because the parents were not married.
If paternity is disputed, however, establishing the parent-child relationship may first be necessary before support can be enforced against the alleged father.

articles.title: K-pop star convicted of violating military service law
articles.summary: The member of K-pop band Winner was given a suspended prison sentence for repeated absences from his national service work.

blocks.text: A South Korean court has handed a suspended one-year prison sentence to K-pop singer Song Min-ho after he was convicted of violating the country's military service law.
The 33-year-old member of the boy band Winner was found to have been absent multiple times at a community centre in Seoul, where he had worked as a social worker from 2023 to 2024.
All able-bodied men in South Korea have to serve at least 18 months in the military. But some are alternatively assigned as social service personnel for health reasons.
The prison sentence handed on Thursday is suspended for two years. That means he can avoid incarceration if he does not commit any crime during that two-year probationary period.
The court heard that Song, who is also known by his stage name Mino, had recorded 102 unauthorised absences during his 21-month stint as a social service agent.
Military service is a duty to be performed "faithfully", and social service agents are "no exception", the court said.
But the court also noted that Song had admitted to the charges and shown remorse.

Authorities launched an investigation into Song shortly after he was discharged in 2024, when local media reported that he was frequently absent from his social service duties and took excessive sick leave.
Song's supervisor at the social service centre was also given a suspended jail sentence for helping him dodge his duties, including falsifying records to make it look like Song had reported to work.
The conscription of South Korea's entertainers has long been a topic of national public debate.

Gangnam Style singer Psy famously had to enlist twice, once in 2003 and another time in 2007, after a Seoul court ruled that he had neglected his duties by continuing his showbiz activities during his first national service stint.

Steve Yoo, one of the country's biggest pop stars in the 1990s and early 2000s, was embroiled in a national scandal after he was found to have evaded military service in 2002. South Korean authorities banned him from the country after he renounced his citizenship and became a US national shortly before he was due to serve in the military.

Going on hiatus to serve in the military is often a threat for budding careers in South Korea's fast-moving entertainment industry. But the evasion of military service also comes with intense public scrutiny and legal repercussions.
Ahead of the ruling on Thursday, Song told reporters that he regretted his actions and was "sorry toward the people who gave me so much love", Seoul Economic Daily reported.
But he did not answer a question about whether he would re-enlist to serve the mandatory duty.

articles.title: DOJ to look into totality of circumstances over Gracioso affidavit
articles.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) will also take into account the credibility and motivation of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. in evaluating his claim that he delivered cash to members of the…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 1:21pm

The Department of Justice (DOJ) will also take into account the credibility and motivation of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. in evaluating his claim that he delivered cash to members of the Duterte family supposedly on the instruction of former Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.

In his affidavit now being evaluated by the department, Gracioso said that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte.
In an interview with GMA News, he said that he also delivered cash to former President Rodrigo Duterte.
Vice President Duterte, however, said she does not know Gracioso, and she did not receive any money from him.

“Mga kababayan (My countrymen), I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him,” Sara Duterte said in a statement over the weekend. “My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him,” she added.
Former President Duterte and Rep. Duterte have yet to comment on the allegations.
Meanwhile, Velasco’s camp has also denied the allegations against the former House leader, describing such as having “no basis.”

“The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested,” said Velasco's spokesperson, Atty. Rowell Ilagan in a statement.

“The ‘one-size-fits-all’ narration by this individual seems to be designed and fabricated to attack as many targets as it can while being inconsistent with verifiable events, that is, the COVID-19 pandemic, Atty. Velasco's period of service as speaker, other details, and even basic common sense.”
‘Totality of circumstances’
According to Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, the DOJ will look at the totality of the circumstances.

“Sa amin ring karanasan, lalo na ‘yung kasama diyan sa mga ganyang ginagawan, hindi naman talaga okay na tao ‘yan, di ba? ‘Yung para sumama ka sa mali na gawain— tulad ng ibang witness kasama sila sa lagayan. Eh, nakipag kontyabahan ka din sa lagayan. Kasama ka doon sa bagman, kasama ka din,” he said.

(In our experience as well, especially those involved in such activities, they are not really good people, right? For you to participate in wrongdoing— like some of the witnesses, they were involved in the payoff. You also colluded in the payoff. You were involved with the bagman, you were also involved.)

“So factor in lahat to. Pero ang factor din dito ‘yung factual setting na ma-verify, mavalidate namin. Tinitignan din namin ‘yung motivation. Kaya nga sa akin, totality. Totality of the circumstances,” he added.

(So we factor all of this in. But another factor here is the factual setting that we can verify and validate. We are also looking at the motivation. That’s why for me, it is the totality. Totality of the circumstances.)
He issued the remark when asked if the DOJ will take into account Gracioso’s credibility and record in evaluating his remark.
Last week, Vida confirmed that the Justice Department has received the affidavit and was evaluating it.
He said they received the affidavit on either Thursday or Friday.
According to Vida, there is currently no request for Gracioso to be placed under the Witness Protection Program.
“Hindi pa ‘yun ang pinaguusapan kasi we need to be able to validate and verify material points of the statement. Mahirap ‘yung palulundagin lang tayo sa patag,” he said.

(That is not yet what we are discussing because we need to be able to validate and verify material points of the statement. It is difficult if we just let ourselves be led on a wild goose chase.) — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: PCG deploys vessel, aircraft to drive away Chinese research ship off Batanes
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Thursday deployed a patrol vessel and an aircraft to drive away a Chinese research vessel allegedly conducting unauthorized marine scientific research off Itbayat,…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 1:07pm

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Thursday deployed a patrol vessel and an aircraft to drive away a Chinese research vessel allegedly conducting unauthorized marine scientific research off Itbayat, Batanes.

In a statement, PCG spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said the JIA HAI KE 7 was conducting unauthorized marine scientific research within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

“Under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, no foreign vessel may conduct marine scientific research in the Philippine EEZ without the express consent of the Philippine government,” he said.

“The Department of Foreign Affairs has confirmed that no such consent was given to JIA HAI KE 7. The PCG will continue to challenge, disrupt, and drive away the vessel until it leaves Philippine waters,” he added.
According to Tarriela, the JIA HAI KE 7 had been operating in waters about 37 nautical miles northwest of Itbayat since the PCG confirmed its presence on September 28.
The PCG deployed BRP Teresa Magbanua (MRRV-9701) and Islander aircraft 251 to the area.
At around 7:55 a.m., BRP Teresa Magbanua approached the JIA HAI KE 7 to within less than 100 yards and deployed a rigid-hull inflatable boat (RHIB), which repeatedly circled the Chinese vessel.
The JIA HAI KE 7 repeatedly maneuvered to evade the Philippine units while BRP Teresa Magbanua issued continuous radio challenges, Tarriela said.
During the operation, China Coast Guard (CCG) vessel 2503 arrived in the area and repeatedly issued radio challenges to BRP Teresa Magbanua.
The Philippine vessel then shadowed CCG-2503 at about 1,000 yards while maintaining its position near the Chinese research vessel.
Tarriela said the involvement of a CCG vessel was significant because the JIA HAI KE 7 is privately owned.
He also raised questions about what data the research vessel may have collected in the area, including near undersea cable corridors in the Luzon Strait.
Meanwhile, Islander 251 took off from Basco Airport to conduct a maritime domain awareness flight over the area. The aircraft circled the vicinity at low altitude in support of BRP Teresa Magbanua.
As of 11 a.m., BRP Teresa Magbanua remained about 37 nautical miles northwest of Itbayat and was circling the JIA HAI KE 7 at about 500 yards.

“This operation is in accordance with the guidance of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. to protect the country's maritime domain and not to tolerate any unauthorized foreign research within Philippine waters,” Tarriela said. — VBL, GMA News
